requirements.title: Privacy Rule text governs over summary guidance
requirements.description: Where any conflict exists between the OCR summary of key elements and the actual Privacy Rule text at 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E, the Rule itself is authoritative and must be followed for compliance determinations.
requirements.quote: In the event of a conflict between this summary and the Rule, the Rule governs.

requirements.title: Applicable regulatory source is 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164 Subparts A and E
requirements.description: The governing regulatory text for HIPAA privacy obligations is 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E; compliance activities must be grounded in that full rule rather than summary material.
requirements.quote: **Full rule:** 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E

requirements.title: National standards for protection of health information
requirements.description: The Privacy Rule establishes a set of national standards for the protection of certain individually identifiable health information, issued by HHS to implement HIPAA's requirements.
requirements.quote: The Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information ("Privacy Rule") establishes, for the first time, a set of national standards for the protection of certain health information.

requirements.title: Covered entities governed on use and disclosure of PHI
requirements.description: Organizations subject to the Privacy Rule, known as covered entities, must comply with standards governing the use and disclosure of individuals' protected health information.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule standards address the use and disclosure of individuals' health information—called "protected health information" by organizations subject to the Privacy Rule — called "covered entities,"

requirements.title: Individual privacy rights over health information
requirements.description: The Privacy Rule sets standards for individuals' privacy rights, enabling them to understand and control how their health information is used.
requirements.quote: as well as standards for individuals' privacy rights to understand and control how their health information is used

requirements.title: OCR implementation and enforcement authority
requirements.description: Within HHS, the Office for Civil Rights is responsible for implementing and enforcing the Privacy Rule through voluntary compliance activities and civil money penalties.
requirements.quote: Within HHS, the Office for Civil Rights ("OCR") has responsibility for implementing and enforcing the Privacy Rule with respect to voluntary compliance activities and civil money penalties.

requirements.title: Balance protection of information with permitted flow of health information
requirements.description: Protection of individuals' health information must be achieved while still allowing the flow of health information needed to provide and promote high quality health care and to protect public health and well being.
requirements.quote: A major goal of the Privacy Rule is to assure that individuals' health information is properly protected while allowing the flow of health information needed to provide and promote high quality health care and to protect the public's health and well being.

requirements.title: HHS Secretary must publicize standards for electronic exchange, privacy and security of health information
requirements.description: HIPAA Sections 261 through 264 impose an obligation on the Secretary of HHS to publicize standards governing the electronic exchange, privacy and security of health information — the Administrative Simplification provisions that form the statutory basis of the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: Sections 261 through 264 of HIPAA require the Secretary of HHS to publicize standards for the electronic exchange, privacy and security of health information.

requirements.title: Privacy Rule as published and subsequently modified is the governing regulation
requirements.description: The controlling regulatory text is the Privacy Rule published December 28, 2000, as amended by the final modifications published August 14, 2002; compliance interpretation must account for both the original rule and the 2002 modifications.
requirements.quote: The final regulation, the Privacy Rule, was published December 28, 2000. In March 2002, the Department proposed modifications; the final modifications were published August 14, 2002.

requirements.title: Privacy Rule applies to defined covered entities
requirements.description: The Privacy Rule and all Administrative Simplification rules apply to health plans, health care clearinghouses, and any health care provider who transmits health information in electronic form in connection with transactions for which HHS has adopted standards under HIPAA. These three classes are the "covered entities".
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule, as well as all the Administrative Simplification rules, apply to health plans, health care clearinghouses, and to any health care provider who transmits health information in electronic form in connection with transactions for which the Secretary of HHS has adopted standards under HIPAA (the "covered entities").

requirements.title: Health plans that provide or pay for medical care are covered entities
requirements.description: Individual and group plans that provide or pay the cost of medical care are covered entities, including health, dental, vision and prescription drug insurers, HMOs, Medicare, Medicaid, Medicare+Choice and Medicare supplement insurers, and long-term care insurers (excluding nursing home fixed-indemnity policies), as well as employer-sponsored, government-sponsored, church-sponsored and multi-employer health plans.
requirements.quote: Individual and group plans that provide or pay the cost of medical care are covered entities.

requirements.title: Small self-administered group health plan exclusion
requirements.description: A group health plan with fewer than 50 participants that is administered solely by the employer that established and maintains the plan is not a covered entity.
requirements.quote: a group health plan with less than 50 participants that is administered solely by the employer that established and maintains the plan is not a covered entity

requirements.title: Government programs whose principal purpose is not health care are not health plans
requirements.description: Government-funded programs whose principal purpose is not providing or paying the cost of health care, such as the food stamps program, are not health plans under the rule.
requirements.quote: those whose principal purpose is not providing or paying the cost of health care, such as the food stamps program

requirements.title: Government programs directly providing health care or granting funds are not health plans
requirements.description: Government-funded programs whose principal activity is directly providing health care (such as a community health center) or making grants to fund the direct provision of health care are not health plans.
requirements.quote: those programs whose principal activity is directly providing health care, such as a community health center, or the making of grants to fund the direct provision of health care

requirements.title: Workers' compensation, auto and property/casualty insurers are not health plans
requirements.description: Entities providing only workers' compensation, automobile insurance, or property and casualty insurance are not health plans and therefore are not covered entities on that basis.
requirements.quote: Certain types of insurance entities are also not health plans, including entities providing only workers' compensation, automobile insurance, and property and casualty insurance.

requirements.title: Provider coverage is independent of provider size
requirements.description: Every health care provider, regardless of size, who electronically transmits health information in connection with certain transactions is a covered entity. Covered transactions include claims, benefit eligibility inquiries, referral authorization requests, or other transactions for which HHS has established standards under the HIPAA Transactions Rule.
requirements.quote: Every health care provider, regardless of size, who electronically transmits health information in connection with certain transactions, is a covered entity.

requirements.title: Use of electronic technology alone does not create covered entity status
requirements.description: Using electronic technology such as email does not by itself make a health care provider a covered entity; the transmission must be in connection with a standard transaction.
requirements.quote: Using electronic technology, such as email, does not mean a health care provider is a covered entity; the transmission must be in connection with a standard transaction.

requirements.title: Coverage applies whether transactions are transmitted directly or through a third party
requirements.description: A health care provider is covered by the Privacy Rule whether it electronically transmits standard transactions directly or uses a billing service or other third party to do so on its behalf.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule covers a health care provider whether it electronically transmits these transactions directly or uses a billing service or other third party to do so on its behalf.

requirements.title: Definition of a health care clearinghouse
requirements.description: Health care clearinghouses are entities that process nonstandard information received from another entity into a standard format or data content, or convert standard information into nonstandard form.
requirements.quote: Health care clearinghouses are entities that process nonstandard information they receive from another entity into a standard (i.e., standard format or data content), or vice versa.

requirements.title: Clearinghouses typically receive identifiable health information as a business associate
requirements.description: In most instances health care clearinghouses receive individually identifiable health information only when providing processing services to a health plan or health care provider as a business associate.
requirements.quote: health care clearinghouses will receive individually identifiable health information only when they are providing these processing services to a health plan or health care provider as a business associate

requirements.title: Entities included as clearinghouses when performing clearinghouse functions
requirements.description: Billing services, repricing companies, community health management information systems, and value-added networks and switches are health care clearinghouses if these entities perform clearinghouse functions.
requirements.quote: Health care clearinghouses include billing services, repricing companies, community health management information systems, and value-added networks and switches if these entities perform clearinghouse functions.

requirements.title: Definition of a business associate
requirements.description: A business associate is a person or organization outside the covered entity's workforce that performs functions or activities on behalf of, or provides services to, a covered entity involving the use or disclosure of individually identifiable health information. Qualifying functions include claims processing, data analysis, utilization review, and billing; qualifying services are limited to legal, actuarial, accounting, consulting, data aggregation, management, administrative, accreditation, or financial services.
requirements.quote: In general, a business associate is a person or organization, other than a member of a covered entity's workforce, that performs certain functions or activities on behalf of, or provides certain services to, a covered entity that involve the use or disclosure of individually identifiable health information.

requirements.title: Exclusion from business associate status for incidental PHI access
requirements.description: Persons or organizations whose functions or services do not involve the use or disclosure of protected health information are not business associates, provided that any access to protected health information by them would be incidental, if at all.
requirements.quote: However, persons or organizations are not considered business associates if their functions or services do not involve the use or disclosure of protected health information, and where any access to protected health information by such persons would be incidental, if at all.

requirements.title: A covered entity may itself be a business associate
requirements.description: One covered entity can be classified as the business associate of another covered entity, and the business associate obligations apply in that relationship.
requirements.quote: A covered entity can be the business associate of another covered entity.

requirements.title: Business associate agreement required before using a non-workforce contractor
requirements.description: When a covered entity engages a contractor or other non-workforce member to perform business associate services or activities, the covered entity must include certain protections for the information in a business associate agreement.
requirements.quote: When a covered entity uses a contractor or other non-workforce member to perform "business associate" services or activities, the Rule requires that the covered entity include certain protections for the information in a business associate agreement.

requirements.title: Contract must impose specified written safeguards on PHI
requirements.description: In the business associate contract, the covered entity must impose specified written safeguards on the individually identifiable health information used or disclosed by its business associates.
requirements.quote: In the business associate contract, a covered entity must impose specified written safeguards on the individually identifiable health information used or disclosed by its business associates.

requirements.title: Contract may not authorize uses or disclosures that violate the Rule
requirements.description: A covered entity is prohibited from contractually authorizing its business associate to make any use or disclosure of protected health information that would violate the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: Moreover, a covered entity may not contractually authorize its business associate to make any use or disclosure of protected health information that would violate the Rule.

requirements.title: PHI protected in all forms and media
requirements.description: All individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by a covered entity or its business associate must be protected as PHI, regardless of form — electronic, paper, or oral.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule protects all "individually identifiable health information" held or transmitted by a covered entity or its business associate, in any form or media, whether electronic, paper, or oral.

requirements.title: Definition of individually identifiable health information
requirements.description: Information, including demographic data, qualifies as individually identifiable health information when it relates to the individual's past, present or future physical or mental health or condition, the provision of health care to the individual, or past, present or future payment for that care, and it identifies the individual or there is a reasonable basis to believe it can be used to identify the individual. Common identifiers such as name, address, birth date and Social Security Number are included.
requirements.quote: and that identifies the individual or for which there is a reasonable basis to believe can be used to identify the individual. Individually identifiable health information includes many common identifiers (e.g., name, address, birth date, Social Security Number).

requirements.title: Employment records excluded from PHI
requirements.description: Employment records that a covered entity maintains in its capacity as an employer are excluded from protected health information.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule excludes from protected health information employment records that a covered entity maintains in its capacity as an employer

requirements.title: FERPA education records excluded from PHI
requirements.description: Education and certain other records subject to, or defined in, the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, 20 U.S.C. §1232g, are excluded from protected health information.
requirements.quote: education and certain other records subject to, or defined in, the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act, 20 U.S.C. §1232g

requirements.title: De-identified information may be used and disclosed without restriction
requirements.description: There are no restrictions on the use or disclosure of de-identified health information, which neither identifies nor provides a reasonable basis to identify an individual.
requirements.quote: There are no restrictions on the use or disclosure of de-identified health information. De-identified health information neither identifies nor provides a reasonable basis to identify an individual.

requirements.title: De-identification by qualified statistician determination
requirements.description: Information may be de-identified through a formal determination by a qualified statistician.
requirements.quote: There are two ways to de-identify information; either: 1) a formal determination by a qualified statistician;

requirements.title: De-identification by removal of specified identifiers
requirements.description: Alternatively, de-identification requires removal of specified identifiers of the individual and of the individual's relatives, household members, and employers; this method is adequate only if the covered entity has no actual knowledge that the remaining information could be used to identify the individual.
requirements.quote: the removal of specified identifiers of the individual and of the individual's relatives, household members, and employers is required, and is adequate only if the covered entity has no actual knowledge that the remaining information could be used to identify the individual

requirements.title: Prohibition on use or disclosure of PHI without permission or authorization
requirements.description: A covered entity is prohibited from using or disclosing protected health information unless the use or disclosure is permitted or required by the Privacy Rule, or the individual who is the subject of the information (or their personal representative) has authorized it in writing.
requirements.quote: A covered entity may not use or disclose protected health information, except either: (1) as the Privacy Rule permits or requires; or (2) as the individual who is the subject of the information (or the individual's personal representative) authorizes in writing.

requirements.title: Written authorization required for non-permitted uses and disclosures
requirements.description: Where a use or disclosure of PHI is not permitted or required by the Privacy Rule, it may proceed only on the written authorization of the individual who is the subject of the information or that individual's personal representative.
requirements.quote: as the individual who is the subject of the information (or the individual's personal representative) authorizes in writing

requirements.title: Required disclosure limited to two situations
requirements.description: A covered entity is required to disclose protected health information in only two situations: to individuals or their personal representatives on request for access or an accounting of disclosures, and to HHS in connection with a compliance investigation, review or enforcement action. All other disclosures are permissive rather than mandatory.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must disclose protected health information in only two situations

requirements.title: Mandatory disclosure to individuals requesting access or an accounting of disclosures
requirements.description: The covered entity must disclose protected health information to individuals, or their personal representatives, specifically when they request access to their PHI or an accounting of disclosures of their PHI.
requirements.quote: to individuals (or their personal representatives) specifically when they request access to, or an accounting of disclosures of, their protected health information
requirements.trigger: The individual requests access to, or an accounting of disclosures of, their protected health information
requirements.happyPath: The individual submits a request for access or an accounting of disclosures; the covered entity identifies the individual's PHI and discloses the requested information or accounting to the individual or their personal representative.

requirements.title: Mandatory disclosure to HHS for compliance and enforcement activity
requirements.description: The covered entity must disclose protected health information to HHS when HHS is undertaking a compliance investigation or review or an enforcement action.
requirements.quote: to HHS when it is undertaking a compliance investigation or review or enforcement action
requirements.trigger: HHS undertakes a compliance investigation, review or enforcement action

requirements.title: Permitted uses and disclosures without authorization
requirements.description: The system must permit, but not require, covered entities to use and disclose PHI without individual authorization for six categories: to the individual; treatment, payment and health care operations; opportunity to agree or object; incident to a permitted use or disclosure; public interest and benefit activities; and limited data set for research, public health or health care operations.
requirements.quote: A covered entity is permitted, but not required, to use and disclose protected health information, without an individual's authorization, for the following purposes or situations: (1) To the Individual; (2) Treatment, Payment, and Health Care Operations; (3) Opportunity to Agree or Object; (4) Incident to an otherwise permitted use and disclosure; (5) Public Interest and Benefit Activities; and (6) Limited Data Set for the purposes of research, public health or health care operations.

requirements.title: Disclosure to the individual who is the subject of the PHI
requirements.description: A covered entity may disclose protected health information to the individual who is the subject of that information, without authorization.
requirements.quote: A covered entity may disclose protected health information to the individual who is the subject of the information.

requirements.title: Use and disclosure for own treatment, payment and health care operations
requirements.description: A covered entity may use and disclose PHI for its own treatment, payment, and health care operations activities.
requirements.quote: A covered entity may use and disclose protected health information for its own treatment, payment, and health care operations activities.

requirements.title: Disclosure for another entity's treatment, payment or specified operations requires prior relationship
requirements.description: PHI may be disclosed for the treatment activities of any health care provider, the payment activities of another covered entity or provider, or the health care operations of another covered entity limited to quality/competency assurance or fraud and abuse detection and compliance activities — only if both covered entities have or had a relationship with the individual and the PHI pertains to that relationship.
requirements.quote: the health care operations of another covered entity involving either quality or competency assurance activities or fraud and abuse detection and compliance activities, if both covered entities have or had a relationship with the individual and the protected health information pertains to the relationship

requirements.title: Definition of treatment
requirements.description: Treatment is defined as the provision, coordination, or management of health care and related services for an individual by one or more providers, including consultation between providers and referral of a patient from one provider to another.
requirements.quote: *Treatment* is the provision, coordination, or management of health care and related services for an individual by one or more health care providers, including consultation between providers regarding a patient and referral of a patient by one provider to another.

requirements.title: Definition of payment
requirements.description: Payment covers health plan activities to obtain premiums, determine or fulfill coverage and benefit responsibilities, and furnish or obtain reimbursement, plus provider activities to obtain payment or be reimbursed for care provided to an individual.
requirements.quote: *Payment* encompasses activities of a health plan to obtain premiums, determine or fulfill responsibilities for coverage and provision of benefits, and furnish or obtain reimbursement for health care delivered to an individual and activities of a health care provider to obtain payment or be reimbursed for the provision of health care to an individual.

requirements.title: Definition of health care operations
requirements.description: Health care operations comprise a closed list of six activity groups: quality assessment/improvement including case management and care coordination; competency assurance including performance evaluation, credentialing and accreditation; medical reviews, audits or legal services including fraud and abuse detection and compliance programs; specified insurance functions such as underwriting, risk rating and reinsuring risk; business planning, development, management and administration; and general administrative activities including de-identification, creating a limited data set, and certain fundraising.
requirements.quote: *Health care operations* are any of the following activities: (a) quality assessment and improvement activities, including case management and care coordination; (b) competency assurance activities, including provider or health plan performance evaluation, credentialing, and accreditation; (c) conducting or arranging for medical reviews, audits, or legal services, including fraud and abuse detection and compliance programs; (d) specified insurance functions, such as underwriting, risk rating, and reinsuring risk; (e) business planning, development, management, and administration; and (f) business management and general administrative activities of the entity

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes require authorization for TPO uses
requirements.description: Most uses and disclosures of psychotherapy notes for treatment, payment, and health care operations purposes require an individual authorization.
requirements.quote: Most uses and disclosures of psychotherapy notes for treatment, payment, and health care operations purposes require an authorization.

requirements.title: Consent for TPO is optional
requirements.description: Obtaining written consent from individuals to use and disclose their PHI for treatment, payment, and health care operations is optional under the Privacy Rule for all covered entities.
requirements.quote: Obtaining "consent" (written permission from individuals to use and disclose their protected health information for treatment, payment, and health care operations) is optional under the Privacy Rule for all covered entities.

requirements.title: Informal permission may be obtained orally or by circumstance
requirements.description: For uses and disclosures requiring an opportunity to agree or object, informal permission may be obtained by asking the individual outright or through circumstances that clearly give the individual the opportunity to agree, acquiesce, or object.
requirements.quote: Informal permission may be obtained by asking the individual outright, or by circumstances that clearly give the individual the opportunity to agree, acquiesce, or object.

requirements.title: Best-interests judgment where individual is incapacitated or unavailable
requirements.description: Where the individual is incapacitated, in an emergency situation, or not available, covered entities may generally make such uses and disclosures if, in the exercise of professional judgment, the use or disclosure is determined to be in the individual's best interests.
requirements.quote: Where the individual is incapacitated, in an emergency situation, or not available, covered entities generally may make such uses and disclosures, if in the exercise of their professional judgment, the use or disclosure is determined to be in the best interests of the individual.

requirements.title: Facility directory disclosures limited to specified data elements
requirements.description: A covered health care provider may rely on informal permission to list the individual's name, general condition, religious affiliation, and location in its facility directory; condition and location may be disclosed to anyone asking for the individual by name, and religious affiliation only to clergy.
requirements.quote: A covered health care provider may rely on an individual's informal permission to list in its facility directory the individual's name, general condition, religious affiliation, and location in the provider's facility. The provider may then disclose the individual's condition and location in the facility to anyone asking for the individual by name, and also may disclose religious affiliation to clergy.

requirements.title: Disclosure to family and others involved in care
requirements.description: A covered entity may rely on an individual's informal permission to disclose to family, relatives, friends, or other identified persons PHI directly relevant to that person's involvement in the individual's care or payment for care.
requirements.quote: A covered entity also may rely on an individual's informal permission to disclose to the individual's family, relatives, or friends, or to other persons whom the individual identifies, protected health information directly relevant to that person's involvement in the individual's care or payment for care.

requirements.title: Notification disclosures of location, condition or death
requirements.description: A covered entity may rely on informal permission to use or disclose PHI to notify family members, personal representatives, or others responsible for the individual's care of the individual's location, general condition, or death.
requirements.quote: a covered entity may rely on an individual's informal permission to use or disclose protected health information for the purpose of notifying family members, personal representatives, or others responsible for the individual's care of the individual's location, general condition, or death

requirements.title: Incidental disclosures permitted with reasonable safeguards and minimum necessary
requirements.description: A use or disclosure occurring incident to an otherwise permitted use or disclosure is permitted so long as the covered entity has adopted reasonable safeguards and the information shared was limited to the minimum necessary; not every risk of incidental disclosure must be eliminated.
requirements.quote: A use or disclosure of this information that occurs as a result of, or as "incident to," an otherwise permitted use or disclosure is permitted as long as the covered entity has adopted reasonable safeguards as required by the Privacy Rule, and the information being shared was limited to the "minimum necessary."

requirements.title: Twelve national priority purposes permitted without authorization
requirements.description: The Privacy Rule permits use and disclosure of PHI without the individual's authorization or permission for 12 national priority purposes.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule permits use and disclosure of protected health information, without an individual's authorization or permission, for 12 national priority purposes.

requirements.title: Disclosures required by law
requirements.description: Covered entities may use and disclose PHI without individual authorization as required by law, including by statute, regulation, or court order.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may use and disclose protected health information without individual authorization as required by law (including by statute, regulation, or court orders).

requirements.title: Public health activity disclosures
requirements.description: PHI may be disclosed to public health authorities authorized to collect it for preventing or controlling disease, injury or disability and to authorities receiving child abuse and neglect reports; to FDA-regulated entities for adverse event reporting, product tracking, recalls and post-marketing surveillance; to individuals possibly exposed to a communicable disease where notification is authorized by law; and to employers regarding work-related illness or injury or workplace medical surveillance when requested.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information to: (1) public health authorities authorized by law to collect or receive such information for preventing or controlling disease, injury, or disability and to public health or other government authorities authorized to receive reports of child abuse and neglect

requirements.title: Disclosures regarding victims of abuse, neglect or domestic violence
requirements.description: In certain circumstances, covered entities may disclose PHI to appropriate government authorities regarding victims of abuse, neglect, or domestic violence.
requirements.quote: In certain circumstances, covered entities may disclose protected health information to appropriate government authorities regarding victims of abuse, neglect, or domestic violence.

requirements.title: Disclosures for health oversight activities
requirements.description: Covered entities may disclose PHI to health oversight agencies for legally authorized health oversight activities such as audits and investigations necessary for oversight of the health care system and government benefit programs.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information to health oversight agencies for purposes of legally authorized health oversight activities, such as audits and investigations necessary for oversight of the health care system and government benefit programs.

requirements.title: Disclosures in judicial and administrative proceedings
requirements.description: PHI may be disclosed in a judicial or administrative proceeding where the request is by order of a court or administrative tribunal, or in response to a subpoena or other lawful process if certain assurances regarding notice to the individual or a protective order are provided.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information in a judicial or administrative proceeding if the request for the information is through an order from a court or administrative tribunal. Such information may also be disclosed in response to a subpoena or other lawful process if certain assurances regarding notice to the individual or a protective order are provided.

requirements.title: Law enforcement disclosures limited to six circumstances
requirements.description: PHI may be disclosed to law enforcement officials only under six specified circumstances and subject to specified conditions: as required by law and administrative requests; to identify or locate a suspect, fugitive, material witness or missing person; in response to a request about a victim or suspected victim of a crime; to alert law enforcement of a death suspected to result from criminal activity; where PHI is evidence of a crime that occurred on the premises; and by a provider in a medical emergency off-premises to inform law enforcement about a crime.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information to law enforcement officials for law enforcement purposes under the following six circumstances, and subject to specified conditions:

requirements.title: Decedent disclosures to funeral directors, coroners and medical examiners
requirements.description: Covered entities may disclose PHI to funeral directors as needed, and to coroners or medical examiners to identify a deceased person, determine cause of death, and perform other functions authorized by law.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information to funeral directors as needed, and to coroners or medical examiners to identify a deceased person, determine the cause of death, and perform other functions authorized by law.

requirements.title: Disclosures for cadaveric organ, eye or tissue donation
requirements.description: Covered entities may use or disclose PHI to facilitate the donation and transplantation of cadaveric organs, eyes, and tissue.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may use or disclose protected health information to facilitate the donation and transplantation of cadaveric organs, eyes, and tissue.

requirements.title: Research use without authorization requires IRB waiver or researcher representations
requirements.description: A covered entity may use and disclose PHI for research without authorization only if it obtains one of: documentation of IRB or Privacy Board approval of an alteration or waiver of authorization; researcher representations that the use is solely preparatory to research, that no PHI will be removed from the covered entity, and that the PHI sought is necessary for the research; or researcher representations that the use is solely for research on decedents' PHI.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule permits a covered entity to use and disclose protected health information for research purposes, without an individual's authorization, provided the covered entity obtains either: (1) documentation that an alteration or waiver of individuals' authorization has been approved by an Institutional Review Board or Privacy Board

requirements.title: Definition of research
requirements.description: Research is defined as any systematic investigation designed to develop or contribute to generalizable knowledge.
requirements.quote: "Research" is any systematic investigation designed to develop or contribute to generalizable knowledge.

requirements.title: Disclosure to avert a serious and imminent threat
requirements.description: Covered entities may disclose PHI they believe necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to a person or the public, where the disclosure is made to someone believed able to prevent or lessen the threat, including the target of the threat.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information that they believe is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to a person or the public, when such disclosure is made to someone they believe can prevent or lessen the threat (including the target of the threat).

requirements.title: Essential government function disclosures without authorization
requirements.description: No authorization is required to use or disclose PHI for certain essential government functions, including assuring proper execution of a military mission, authorized intelligence and national security activities, protective services to the President, medical suitability determinations for U.S. State Department employees, protecting health and safety of inmates or correctional employees, and determining eligibility or enrollment in certain government benefit programs.
requirements.quote: An authorization is not required to use or disclose protected health information for certain essential government functions.

requirements.title: Workers' compensation disclosures
requirements.description: Covered entities may disclose PHI as authorized by, and to comply with, workers' compensation laws and other similar programs providing benefits for work-related injuries or illnesses.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may disclose protected health information as authorized by, and to comply with, workers' compensation laws and other similar programs providing benefits for work-related injuries or illnesses.

requirements.title: Limited data set definition and identifier removal
requirements.description: A limited data set is PHI from which certain specified direct identifiers of individuals and their relatives, household members, and employers have been removed.
requirements.quote: A limited data set is protected health information from which certain specified direct identifiers of individuals and their relatives, household members, and employers have been removed.

requirements.title: Limited data set use conditioned on a data use agreement
requirements.description: A limited data set may be used and disclosed only for research, health care operations, and public health purposes, and only if the recipient enters into a data use agreement promising specified safeguards for the PHI in the limited data set.
requirements.quote: A limited data set may be used and disclosed for research, health care operations, and public health purposes, provided the recipient enters into a data use agreement promising specified safeguards for the protected health information within the limited data set.

requirements.title: Written authorization required for non-TPO uses and disclosures
requirements.description: The covered entity must obtain the individual's written authorization before any use or disclosure of protected health information that is not for treatment, payment or health care operations, or otherwise permitted or required by the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must obtain the individual's written authorization for any use or disclosure of protected health information that is not for treatment, payment or health care operations or otherwise permitted or required by the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: No conditioning of treatment or benefits on granting authorization
requirements.description: A covered entity may not make treatment, payment, enrollment, or benefits eligibility contingent on the individual granting an authorization, except in limited circumstances.
requirements.quote: A covered entity may not condition treatment, payment, enrollment, or benefits eligibility on an individual granting an authorization, except in limited circumstances.

requirements.title: Authorization must be specific and in plain language with required elements
requirements.description: Every authorization must be written in specific terms and in plain language, and must contain the information to be disclosed or used, the person(s) disclosing and receiving the information, an expiration, the right to revoke in writing, and other required data.
requirements.quote: All authorizations must be in plain language, and contain specific information regarding the information to be disclosed or used, the person(s) disclosing and receiving the information, expiration, right to revoke in writing, and other data.

requirements.title: Disclosures to insurers, employers and pharmaceutical firms require authorization
requirements.description: Disclosures to a life insurer for coverage purposes, disclosures to an employer of pre-employment physical or lab test results, and disclosures to a pharmaceutical firm for its own marketing purposes each require the individual's authorization.
requirements.quote: Examples of disclosures that would require an individual's authorization include disclosures to a life insurer for coverage purposes, disclosures to an employer of the results of a pre-employment physical or lab test, or disclosures to a pharmaceutical firm for their own marketing purposes.

requirements.title: Authorization required to use or disclose psychotherapy notes
requirements.description: A covered entity must obtain the individual's authorization to use or disclose psychotherapy notes, subject to the enumerated exceptions.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must obtain an individual's authorization to use or disclose psychotherapy notes with the following exceptions:

requirements.title: Originator may use psychotherapy notes for treatment
requirements.description: The covered entity that originated the psychotherapy notes may use them for treatment without obtaining authorization.
requirements.quote: The covered entity who originated the notes may use them for treatment.

requirements.title: Permitted uses of psychotherapy notes without authorization
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes may be used or disclosed without authorization for the covered entity's own training, to defend itself in legal proceedings brought by the individual, for HHS compliance investigations, to avert a serious and imminent threat to public health or safety, to a health oversight agency for lawful oversight of the originator, for lawful coroner or medical examiner activities, or as required by law.
requirements.quote: A covered entity may use or disclose, without an individual's authorization, the psychotherapy notes, for its own training, and to defend itself in legal proceedings brought by the individual, for HHS to investigate or determine the covered entity's compliance with the Privacy Rules, to avert a serious and imminent threat to public health or safety, to a health oversight agency for lawful oversight of the originator of the psychotherapy notes, for the lawful activities of a coroner or medical examiner or as required by law.

requirements.title: Definition of marketing
requirements.description: Marketing is defined as any communication about a product or service that encourages recipients to purchase or use the product or service.
requirements.quote: Marketing is any communication about a product or service that encourages recipients to purchase or use the product or service.

requirements.title: Carve-out: communications about the entity's own health-related products or services
requirements.description: Communications that describe health-related products or services, or payment for them, provided by or included in a benefit plan of the covered entity making the communication are not marketing.
requirements.quote: Communications to describe health-related products or services, or payment for them, provided by or included in a benefit plan of the covered entity making the communication;

requirements.title: Carve-out: communications about network providers and plan enhancements
requirements.description: Communications about participating providers in a provider or health plan network, replacement of or enhancements to a health plan, and health-related products or services available only to a health plan's enrollees that add value to but are not part of the benefits plan are not marketing.
requirements.quote: Communications about participating providers in a provider or health plan network, replacement of or enhancements to a health plan, and health-related products or services available only to a health plan's enrollees that add value to, but are not part of, the benefits plan;

requirements.title: Carve-out: communications for treatment of the individual
requirements.description: Communications for treatment of the individual fall outside the definition of marketing and therefore do not require a marketing authorization.
requirements.quote: Communications for treatment of the individual; and

requirements.title: Carve-out: case management and care coordination communications
requirements.description: Communications for case management or care coordination for the individual, or to direct or recommend alternative treatments, therapies, health care providers, or care settings to the individual, are not marketing.
requirements.quote: Communications for case management or care coordination for the individual, or to direct or recommend alternative treatments, therapies, health care providers, or care settings to the individual.

requirements.title: Authorization required for marketing uses of PHI, with two exceptions
requirements.description: A covered entity must obtain an authorization to use or disclose protected health information for marketing, except for face-to-face marketing communications between a covered entity and an individual and for the provision of promotional gifts of nominal value.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must obtain an authorization to use or disclose protected health information for marketing, except for face-to-face marketing communications between a covered entity and an individual, and for a covered entity's provision of promotional gifts of nominal value.

requirements.title: Marketing authorization must disclose third-party remuneration
requirements.description: Where a marketing use involves the covered entity's receipt of direct or indirect remuneration from a third party, the authorization must reveal that fact.
requirements.quote: An authorization for marketing that involves the covered entity's receipt of direct or indirect remuneration from a third party must reveal that fact.

requirements.title: Apply minimum necessary standard to uses, disclosures and requests of PHI
requirements.description: The covered entity must make reasonable efforts to use, disclose, and request only the minimum amount of protected health information needed to accomplish the intended purpose of the use, disclosure, or request.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must make reasonable efforts to use, disclose, and request only the minimum amount of protected health information needed to accomplish the intended purpose of the use, disclosure, or request.

requirements.title: Maintain policies and procedures limiting uses and disclosures to minimum necessary
requirements.description: The covered entity must develop and implement documented policies and procedures that reasonably limit uses and disclosures of PHI to the minimum necessary.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must develop and implement policies and procedures to reasonably limit uses and disclosures to the minimum necessary.

requirements.title: Entire medical record may not be used or disclosed without specific justification
requirements.description: Where the minimum necessary standard applies, the covered entity may not use, disclose or request the entire medical record for a purpose unless it can specifically justify the whole record as the amount reasonably needed for that purpose.
requirements.quote: a covered entity may not use, disclose, or request the entire medical record for a particular purpose, unless it can specifically justify the whole record as the amount reasonably needed for the purpose

requirements.title: Exception: treatment disclosures to or requests by a health care provider
requirements.description: The minimum necessary requirement does not apply to a disclosure to, or a request by, a health care provider for treatment.
requirements.quote: (a) disclosure to or a request by a health care provider for treatment

requirements.title: Exception: disclosure to the individual or personal representative
requirements.description: The minimum necessary requirement does not apply to a disclosure to the individual who is the subject of the information, or that individual's personal representative.
requirements.quote: (b) disclosure to an individual who is the subject of the information, or the individual's personal representative

requirements.title: Exception: uses and disclosures made pursuant to an authorization
requirements.description: The minimum necessary requirement does not apply to a use or disclosure made pursuant to an individual's authorization.
requirements.quote: (c) use or disclosure made pursuant to an authorization

requirements.title: Exception: disclosure to HHS for investigation or enforcement
requirements.description: The minimum necessary requirement does not apply to disclosures to HHS for complaint investigation, compliance review or enforcement.
requirements.quote: (d) disclosure to HHS for complaint investigation, compliance review or enforcement

requirements.title: Exception: uses and disclosures required by law
requirements.description: The minimum necessary requirement does not apply to a use or disclosure that is required by law.
requirements.quote: (e) use or disclosure that is required by law

requirements.title: Exception: uses and disclosures required for HIPAA Administrative Simplification compliance
requirements.description: The minimum necessary requirement does not apply to a use or disclosure required for compliance with the HIPAA Transactions Rule or other HIPAA Administrative Simplification Rules.
requirements.quote: (f) use or disclosure required for compliance with the HIPAA Transactions Rule or other HIPAA Administrative Simplification Rules

requirements.title: Role-based restriction of internal access to PHI
requirements.description: For internal uses, the covered entity must develop and implement policies and procedures that restrict access to and uses of protected health information based on the specific roles of workforce members.
requirements.quote: For internal uses, a covered entity must develop and implement policies and procedures that restrict access and uses of protected health information based on the specific roles of the members of their workforce.

requirements.title: Access policies identify persons, PHI categories and conditions of access
requirements.description: Internal access policies and procedures must identify the persons or classes of persons in the workforce needing access, the categories of PHI to which access is needed, and any conditions under which the information is needed to do their jobs.
requirements.quote: These policies and procedures must identify the persons, or classes of persons, in the workforce who need access to protected health information to carry out their duties, the categories of protected health information to which access is needed, and any conditions under which they need the information to do their jobs.

requirements.title: Standing policies for routine, recurring disclosures and requests
requirements.description: Covered entities must establish and implement policies and procedures for routine, recurring disclosures or requests for disclosures that limit the PHI disclosed to the minimum amount reasonably necessary.
requirements.quote: Covered entities must establish and implement policies and procedures for routine, recurring disclosures, or requests for disclosures, that limits the protected health information disclosed to that which is the minimum amount reasonably necessary.

requirements.title: No individual review required for routine disclosures
requirements.description: For routine, recurring disclosures governed by established policies and procedures, individual review of each disclosure is not required.
requirements.quote: Individual review of each disclosure is not required.

requirements.title: Criteria and individual review for non-routine disclosures and requests
requirements.description: For non-routine, non-recurring disclosures or requests for disclosures, the covered entity must develop criteria designed to limit disclosures to the information reasonably necessary for the purpose, and must review each such request individually against those criteria.
requirements.quote: covered entities must develop criteria designed to limit disclosures to the information reasonably necessary to accomplish the purpose of the disclosure and review each of these requests individually in accordance with the established criteria

requirements.title: Reasonable reliance on another covered entity's request
requirements.description: When another covered entity requests protected health information, the covered entity may rely, if reasonable under the circumstances, on that request as complying with the minimum necessary standard.
requirements.quote: If another covered entity makes a request for protected health information, a covered entity may rely, if reasonable under the circumstances, on the request as complying with this minimum necessary standard.

requirements.title: Provide a notice of privacy practices
requirements.description: Each covered entity, subject to certain exceptions, must provide a notice of its privacy practices to individuals.
requirements.quote: Each covered entity, with certain exceptions, must provide a notice of its privacy practices.

requirements.title: Notice describes permitted uses and disclosures of PHI
requirements.description: The privacy practices notice must describe the ways in which the covered entity may use and disclose protected health information.
requirements.quote: The notice must describe the ways in which the covered entity may use and disclose protected health information.

requirements.title: Notice states the covered entity's privacy duties
requirements.description: The notice must state the covered entity's duties to protect privacy, to provide a notice of privacy practices, and to abide by the terms of the current notice.
requirements.quote: The notice must state the covered entity's duties to protect privacy, provide a notice of privacy practices, and abide by the terms of the current notice.

requirements.title: Notice describes individual rights including right to complain
requirements.description: The notice must describe individuals' rights, including the right to complain to HHS and to the covered entity about suspected privacy violations.
requirements.quote: The notice must describe individuals' rights, including the right to complain to HHS and to the covered entity if they believe their privacy rights have been violated.

requirements.title: Notice includes a point of contact for information and complaints
requirements.description: The notice must identify a point of contact for further information and for making complaints to the covered entity.
requirements.quote: The notice must include a point of contact for further information and for making complaints to the covered entity.

requirements.title: Covered entities act in accordance with their notices
requirements.description: Covered entities must conduct their uses and disclosures consistently with the terms of their published privacy practices notice.
requirements.quote: Covered entities must act in accordance with their notices.

requirements.title: Deliver notice no later than first service encounter by channel-appropriate means
requirements.description: A direct treatment provider must deliver the notice not later than the first service encounter: by personal delivery for patient visits, by automatic and contemporaneous electronic response for electronic service delivery, and by prompt mailing for telephonic service delivery.
requirements.quote: Not later than the first service encounter by personal delivery (for patient visits), by automatic and contemporaneous electronic response (for electronic service delivery), and by prompt mailing (for telephonic service delivery)

requirements.title: Post notice prominently at each service delivery site
requirements.description: The provider must post the privacy practices notice at each service delivery site in a clear and prominent place where people seeking service may reasonably be expected to read it.
requirements.quote: By posting the notice at each service delivery site in a clear and prominent place where people seeking service may reasonably be expected to be able to read the notice

requirements.title: Furnish notice after an emergency abates
requirements.description: In emergency treatment situations, the provider must furnish its privacy practices notice as soon as practicable after the emergency abates.
requirements.quote: In emergency treatment situations, the provider must furnish its notice as soon as practicable after the emergency abates.

requirements.title: Publish notice electronically on customer service or benefits web site
requirements.description: A covered entity must make its privacy practices notice electronically available on any web site it maintains for customer service or benefits information.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must also make its notice electronically available on any web site it maintains for customer service or benefits information.

requirements.title: Health plan distributes notice to all enrollees by compliance date
requirements.description: A health plan must distribute its privacy practices notice to each of its enrollees by its Privacy Rule compliance date.
requirements.quote: A health plan must distribute its privacy practices notice to each of its enrollees by its Privacy Rule compliance date.

requirements.title: Notice to new enrollees and triennial availability reminder
requirements.description: After the compliance date, the health plan must give its notice to each new enrollee at enrollment and send a reminder to every enrollee at least once every three years that the notice is available upon request.
requirements.quote: Thereafter, the health plan must give its notice to each new enrollee at enrollment, and send a reminder to every enrollee at least once every three years that the notice is available upon request.

requirements.title: Good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgement of notice receipt
requirements.description: A covered health care provider with a direct treatment relationship must make a good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgement from patients that they received the privacy practices notice.
requirements.quote: A covered health care provider with a direct treatment relationship with individuals must make a good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgement from patients of receipt of the privacy practices notice.

requirements.title: Document reason for failure to obtain acknowledgement
requirements.description: The provider must document the reason for any failure to obtain the patient's written acknowledgement of notice receipt.
requirements.quote: The provider must document the reason for any failure to obtain the patient's written acknowledgement.

requirements.title: Acknowledgement not required in emergency treatment
requirements.description: The provider is relieved of the need to request written acknowledgement of notice receipt in an emergency treatment situation.
requirements.quote: The provider is relieved of the need to request acknowledgement in an emergency treatment situation.

requirements.title: Individual right to review and obtain a copy of PHI
requirements.description: Except in certain circumstances, individuals have the right to review and obtain a copy of their protected health information held in a covered entity's designated record set.
requirements.quote: Except in certain circumstances, individuals have the right to review and obtain a copy of their protected health information in a covered entity's designated record set.

requirements.title: Individual requests access to their designated record set
requirements.description: An individual submits an access request and the covered entity provides review of and a copy of the PHI in the designated record set, applying exceptions, denial rules, review rights and cost-based fees as applicable.
requirements.quote: For information included within the right of access, covered entities may deny an individual access in certain specified situations, such as when a health care professional believes access could cause harm to the individual or another.
requirements.trigger: Individual requests to review or obtain a copy of their protected health information
requirements.happyPath: Individual submits an access request; covered entity locates the PHI in the designated record set; confirms the information is not within an access exception; provides review and a copy; charges only reasonable, cost-based copying and postage fees.

requirements.title: Definition of designated record set
requirements.description: The designated record set is the group of records maintained by or for a covered entity used in whole or part to make decisions about individuals, or a provider's medical and billing records, or a health plan's enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems.
requirements.quote: The "designated record set" is that group of records maintained by or for a covered entity that is used, in whole or part, to make decisions about individuals, or that is a provider's medical and billing records about individuals or a health plan's enrollment, payment, claims adjudication, and case or medical management record systems.

requirements.title: Information excepted from the right of access
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes, information compiled for legal proceedings, laboratory results to which CLIA prohibits access, and information held by certain research laboratories are excepted from the right of access.
requirements.quote: The Rule excepts from the right of access the following protected health information: psychotherapy notes, information compiled for legal proceedings, laboratory results to which the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Act (CLIA) prohibits access, or information held by certain research laboratories.

requirements.title: Denial of access where harm is anticipated
requirements.description: For information within the right of access, a covered entity may deny access in certain specified situations, such as when a health care professional believes access could cause harm to the individual or another.
requirements.quote: covered entities may deny an individual access in certain specified situations, such as when a health care professional believes access could cause harm to the individual or another

requirements.title: Right to review of access denial by a licensed professional
requirements.description: Where access is denied on such grounds, the individual must be given the right to have the denial reviewed by a licensed health care professional for a second opinion.
requirements.quote: In such situations, the individual must be given the right to have such denials reviewed by a licensed health care professional for a second opinion.

requirements.title: Access fees limited to reasonable, cost-based copying and postage
requirements.description: Covered entities may impose only reasonable, cost-based fees for the cost of copying and postage when fulfilling access requests.
requirements.quote: Covered entities may impose reasonable, cost-based fees for the cost of copying and postage.

requirements.title: Individual right to amendment of inaccurate or incomplete PHI
requirements.description: Individuals have the right to have covered entities amend their protected health information in a designated record set when that information is inaccurate or incomplete.
requirements.quote: The Rule gives individuals the right to have covered entities amend their protected health information in a designated record set when that information is inaccurate or incomplete.

requirements.title: Propagate accepted amendments to identified and reliant persons
requirements.description: If a covered entity accepts an amendment request, it must make reasonable efforts to provide the amendment to persons the individual identified as needing it and to persons the covered entity knows might rely on the information to the individual's detriment.
requirements.quote: If a covered entity accepts an amendment request, it must make reasonable efforts to provide the amendment to persons that the individual has identified as needing it, and to persons that the covered entity knows might rely on the information to the individual's detriment.

requirements.title: Written denial and statement of disagreement for rejected amendments
requirements.description: If an amendment request is denied, the covered entity must provide the individual with a written denial and allow the individual to submit a statement of disagreement for inclusion in the record.
requirements.quote: If the request is denied, covered entities must provide the individual with a written denial and allow the individual to submit a statement of disagreement for inclusion in the record.

requirements.title: Amend PHI upon notice from another covered entity
requirements.description: A covered entity must amend protected health information in its designated record set upon receipt of a notice to amend from another covered entity.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must amend protected health information in its designated record set upon receipt of notice to amend from another covered entity.

requirements.title: Individual right to an accounting of disclosures
requirements.description: Individuals have a right to an accounting of the disclosures of their protected health information made by a covered entity or its business associates.
requirements.quote: Individuals have a right to an accounting of the disclosures of their protected health information by a covered entity or the covered entity's business associates.

requirements.title: Six-year maximum disclosure accounting period
requirements.description: The maximum disclosure accounting period is the six years immediately preceding the accounting request, and a covered entity need not account for disclosures made before its Privacy Rule compliance date.
requirements.quote: The maximum disclosure accounting period is the six years immediately preceding the accounting request, except a covered entity is not obligated to account for any disclosure made before its Privacy Rule compliance date.

requirements.title: Disclosures excluded from accounting requirement
requirements.description: Accounting is not required for disclosures for treatment, payment or health care operations; to the individual or personal representative; for notification, disaster relief or facility directories; pursuant to an authorization; of a limited data set; for national security or intelligence; to correctional institutions or law enforcement for certain custody purposes; or incident to otherwise permitted or required uses or disclosures.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule does not require accounting for disclosures: (a) for treatment, payment, or health care operations; (b) to the individual or the individual's personal representative

requirements.title: Individual right to request restrictions on use or disclosure
requirements.description: Individuals may request that a covered entity restrict use or disclosure of PHI for treatment, payment or health care operations, disclosure to persons involved in their care or payment, or disclosure notifying family or others about their general condition, location or death.
requirements.quote: Individuals have the right to request that a covered entity restrict use or disclosure of protected health information for treatment, payment or health care operations, disclosure to persons involved in the individual's health care or payment for health care, or disclosure to notify family members or others about the individual's general condition, location, or death.

requirements.title: No obligation to agree to a restriction request
requirements.description: A covered entity is under no obligation to agree to an individual's request for restrictions on use or disclosure.
requirements.quote: A covered entity is under no obligation to agree to requests for restrictions.

requirements.title: Agreed restrictions must be honored except in a medical emergency
requirements.description: A covered entity that agrees to a restriction must comply with the agreed restriction, except for purposes of treating the individual in a medical emergency.
requirements.quote: A covered entity that does agree must comply with the agreed restrictions, except for purposes of treating the individual in a medical emergency.

requirements.title: Permit requests for confidential communications
requirements.description: Health plans and covered health care providers must permit individuals to request an alternative means or location for receiving communications of protected health information, other than those the entity typically employs.
requirements.quote: Health plans and covered health care providers must permit individuals to request an alternative means or location for receiving communications of protected health information by means other than those that the covered entity typically employs.

requirements.title: Health plans accommodate reasonable requests where disclosure could endanger the individual
requirements.description: Health plans must accommodate reasonable requests for confidential communications if the individual indicates that disclosure of all or part of the protected health information could endanger them.
requirements.quote: Health plans must accommodate reasonable requests if the individual indicates that the disclosure of all or part of the protected health information could endanger the individual.

requirements.title: Health plan may not question a statement of endangerment
requirements.description: The health plan may not question the individual's statement that disclosure could endanger them when handling a confidential communications request.
requirements.quote: The health plan may not question the individual's statement of endangerment.

requirements.title: Scalable, entity-appropriate compliance implementation
requirements.description: The Privacy Rule is intended to be flexible and scalable so covered entities of any size can analyze their own needs and implement solutions appropriate for their own environment.
requirements.quote: Therefore the flexibility and scalability of the Rule are intended to allow covered entities to analyze their own needs and implement solutions appropriate for their own environment.

requirements.title: Written privacy policies and procedures
requirements.description: A covered entity must develop and implement written privacy policies and procedures consistent with the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must develop and implement written privacy policies and procedures that are consistent with the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: Designate a privacy official
requirements.description: A covered entity must designate a privacy official responsible for developing and implementing its privacy policies and procedures.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must designate a privacy official responsible for developing and implementing its privacy policies and procedures

requirements.title: Designate a contact person or office for complaints and privacy information
requirements.description: A covered entity must designate a contact person or contact office responsible for receiving complaints and providing individuals with information on its privacy practices.
requirements.quote: and a contact person or contact office responsible for receiving complaints and providing individuals with information on the covered entity's privacy practices

requirements.title: Workforce definition includes unpaid persons under direct control
requirements.description: Workforce members include employees, volunteers, trainees, and may include other persons whose conduct is under the direct control of the entity, whether or not paid by the entity.
requirements.quote: Workforce members include employees, volunteers, trainees, and may also include other persons whose conduct is under the direct control of the entity (whether or not they are paid by the entity).

requirements.title: Train all workforce members on privacy policies
requirements.description: A covered entity must train all workforce members on its privacy policies and procedures, as necessary and appropriate for them to carry out their functions.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must train all workforce members on its privacy policies and procedures, as necessary and appropriate for them to carry out their functions.

requirements.title: Apply sanctions against violating workforce members
requirements.description: A covered entity must have and apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who violate its privacy policies and procedures or the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must have and apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who violate its privacy policies and procedures or the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: Mitigate harmful effects of improper use or disclosure
requirements.description: A covered entity must mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect it learns was caused by a use or disclosure of PHI by its workforce or business associates in violation of its privacy policies or the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect it learns was caused by use or disclosure of protected health information by its workforce or its business associates in violation of its privacy policies and procedures or the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: Maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards
requirements.description: A covered entity must maintain reasonable and appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to prevent intentional or unintentional use or disclosure of PHI in violation of the Privacy Rule and to limit incidental use and disclosure pursuant to otherwise permitted or required uses.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must maintain reasonable and appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to prevent intentional or unintentional use or disclosure of protected health information in violation of the Privacy Rule and to limit its incidental use and disclosure pursuant to otherwise permitted or required use or disclosure.

requirements.title: Example physical safeguards for PHI
requirements.description: Acceptable safeguards may include shredding documents containing PHI before discarding, securing medical records with lock and key or pass code, and limiting access to keys or pass codes.
requirements.quote: such safeguards might include shredding documents containing protected health information before discarding them, securing medical records with lock and key or pass code, and limiting access to keys or pass codes

requirements.title: Complaint procedures for individuals
requirements.description: A covered entity must have procedures for individuals to complain about its compliance with its privacy policies and procedures and the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must have procedures for individuals to complain about its compliance with its privacy policies and procedures and the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: Explain complaint procedures in the privacy practices notice
requirements.description: The covered entity must explain its complaint procedures in its notice of privacy practices, identify to whom complaints can be submitted, and advise that complaints can also be submitted to the Secretary of HHS.
requirements.quote: Among other things, the covered entity must identify to whom individuals can submit complaints to at the covered entity and advise that complaints also can be submitted to the Secretary of HHS.

requirements.title: Ban on retaliation
requirements.description: A covered entity may not retaliate against a person for exercising Privacy Rule rights, assisting in an HHS or other authority investigation, or opposing an act or practice the person believes in good faith violates the Privacy Rule.
