requirements.quote: A covered entity may not retaliate against a person for exercising rights provided by the Privacy Rule, for assisting in an investigation by HHS or another appropriate authority, or for opposing an act or practice that the person believes in good faith violates the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: No waiver of rights as a condition of treatment or benefits
requirements.description: A covered entity may not require an individual to waive any right under the Privacy Rule as a condition for obtaining treatment, payment, and enrollment or benefits eligibility.
requirements.quote: A covered entity may not require an individual to waive any right under the Privacy Rule as a condition for obtaining treatment, payment, and enrollment or benefits eligibility.

requirements.title: Six-year documentation retention
requirements.description: A covered entity must maintain its privacy policies and procedures, privacy practices notices, disposition of complaints, and other required documentation until six years after the later of the date of creation or last effective date.
requirements.quote: A covered entity must maintain, until six years after the later of the date of their creation or last effective date, its privacy policies and procedures, its privacy practices notices, disposition of complaints, and other actions, activities, and designations that the Privacy Rule requires to be documented.

requirements.title: Fully-insured group health plan administrative exception
requirements.description: A fully-insured group health plan that has no more than enrollment data and summary health information need only comply with the ban on retaliatory acts and waiver of individual rights, and the documentation requirements with respect to plan documents.
requirements.quote: The only administrative obligations with which a fully-insured group health plan that has no more than enrollment data and summary health information is required to comply are the (1) ban on retaliatory acts and waiver of individual rights, and (2) documentation requirements with respect to plan documents.

requirements.title: Hybrid entity election with written designation of health care components
requirements.description: A single legal entity covered entity that conducts both covered and non-covered functions may elect hybrid entity status, but must designate in writing the operations performing covered functions as one or more health care components.
requirements.quote: To be a hybrid entity, the covered entity must designate in writing its operations that perform covered functions as one or more "health care components."

requirements.title: Privacy Rule scope limited to designated health care components
requirements.description: Once a hybrid entity designation is made, most Privacy Rule requirements apply only to the designated health care components.
requirements.quote: After making this designation, most of the requirements of the Privacy Rule will apply only to the health care components.

requirements.title: Entity without hybrid designation is subject in its entirety
requirements.description: A covered entity that does not designate health care components is subject to the Privacy Rule across its entire organization.
requirements.quote: A covered entity that does not make this designation is subject in its entirety to the Privacy Rule.

requirements.title: Affiliated covered entity designation must be in writing
requirements.description: Legally separate covered entities affiliated by common ownership or control may designate themselves, including their health care components, as a single covered entity for Privacy Rule compliance; the designation must be documented in writing.
requirements.quote: Legally separate covered entities that are affiliated by common ownership or control may designate themselves (including their health care components) as a single covered entity for Privacy Rule compliance. The designation must be in writing.

requirements.title: PHI sharing within an organized health care arrangement
requirements.description: Covered entities participating in an organized health care arrangement may share protected health information with each other for the arrangement's joint health care operations.
requirements.quote: Covered entities in an organized health care arrangement can share protected health information with each other for the arrangement's joint health care operations.

requirements.title: Each covered function must comply with its applicable provisions
requirements.description: A covered entity performing multiple covered functions must operate each function in compliance with the Privacy Rule provisions applicable to that function.
requirements.quote: A covered entity that performs multiple covered functions must operate its different covered functions in compliance with the Privacy Rule provisions applicable to those covered functions.

requirements.title: Prohibition on cross-function use of PHI where individual is not involved
requirements.description: PHI of an individual receiving services from one covered function may not be used or disclosed for another covered function if the individual is not involved with that other function.
requirements.quote: The covered entity may not use or disclose the protected health information of an individual who receives services from one covered function for another covered function if the individual is not involved with the other function.

requirements.title: Disclosure of enrollment or disenrollment information to plan sponsor
requirements.description: A group health plan and its insurer or HMO may disclose enrollment or disenrollment information with respect to the group health plan or the insurer/HMO offered by the plan to the plan sponsor.
requirements.quote: Enrollment or disenrollment information with respect to the group health plan or a health insurer or HMO offered by the plan.

requirements.title: Disclosure of summary health information for premium bids or plan changes
requirements.description: On request by the plan sponsor, summary health information may be disclosed for the sponsor to obtain premium bids for coverage through the group health plan, or to modify, amend or terminate the plan.
requirements.quote: If requested by the plan sponsor, summary health information for the plan sponsor to use to obtain premium bids for providing health insurance coverage through the group health plan, or to modify, amend, or terminate the group health plan.

requirements.title: Certification of amended plan document required before plan administration disclosures
requirements.description: Before disclosing enrollees' PHI to a plan sponsor for plan administration functions, the group health plan must receive certification from the plan sponsor that the plan document has been amended to impose use and disclosure restrictions.
requirements.quote: The plan must receive certification from the plan sponsor that the group health plan document has been amended to impose restrictions on the plan sponsor's use and disclosure of the protected health information.

requirements.title: Plan sponsor representation barring employment-related use of PHI
requirements.description: The plan document restrictions must include a representation that the plan sponsor will not use or disclose the PHI for any employment-related action or decision, or in connection with any other benefit plan.
requirements.quote: These restrictions must include the representation that the plan sponsor will not use or disclose the protected health information for any employment-related action or decision or in connection with any other benefit plan.

requirements.title: Treat personal representatives as the individual
requirements.description: A covered entity must treat a person legally authorized as a "personal representative" identically to the individual for all uses and disclosures of the individual's PHI and for the exercise of the individual's rights under the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule requires a covered entity to treat a "personal representative" the same as the individual, with respect to uses and disclosures of the individual's protected health information, as well as the individual's rights under the Rule.

requirements.title: Definition of a personal representative
requirements.description: A personal representative is a person legally authorized to make health care decisions on an individual's behalf, or to act for a deceased individual or that individual's estate. Systems and staff must verify this legal authority before granting representative status.
requirements.quote: A personal representative is a person legally authorized to make health care decisions on an individual's behalf or to act for a deceased individual or the estate.

requirements.title: Abuse, neglect or endangerment exception to representative status
requirements.description: A covered entity may decline to treat a person as the personal representative where it has a reasonable belief that the person may be abusing or neglecting the individual, or that treating the person as the personal representative could otherwise endanger the individual.
requirements.quote: The Privacy Rule permits an exception when a covered entity has a reasonable belief that the personal representative may be abusing or neglecting the individual, or that treating the person as the personal representative could otherwise endanger the individual.

requirements.title: Parents are the default personal representatives of minor children
requirements.description: By default, parents are treated as the personal representatives of their minor children and may therefore exercise individual rights, including access to the medical record, on the child's behalf.
requirements.quote: In most cases, parents are the personal representatives for their minor children. Therefore, in most cases, parents can exercise individual rights, such as access to the medical record, on behalf of their minor children.

requirements.title: Defer to State law where the parent is not the personal representative
requirements.description: In exceptional cases where the parent is not considered the personal representative, the rights of parents to access and control their minor child's PHI are determined by State and other applicable law rather than the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: In these situations, the Privacy Rule defers to State and other law to determine the rights of parents to access and control the protected health information of their minor children.

requirements.title: Licensed professional judgment where State law is silent on parental access
requirements.description: Where State and other law is silent on parental access to a minor's PHI, the covered entity has discretion to grant or deny access, but the decision must be made by a licensed health care professional exercising professional judgment.
requirements.quote: If State and other law is silent concerning parental access to the minor's protected health information, a covered entity has discretion to provide or deny a parent access to the minor's health information, provided the decision is made by a licensed health care professional in the exercise of professional judgment.
requirements.trigger: A parent requests access to a minor child's protected health information and State law is silent on parental access
requirements.happyPath: The access request is routed to a licensed health care professional, who exercises professional judgment, records the decision to provide or deny access, and the outcome is communicated to the parent.

requirements.title: Federal preemption of contrary State privacy laws
requirements.description: State laws that are contrary to the Privacy Rule are preempted by the federal requirements, and the federal requirements apply instead. A State law is 'contrary' when a covered entity could not comply with both the State and federal requirements, or when the State provision is an obstacle to accomplishing the full purposes and objectives of HIPAA's Administrative Simplification provisions.
requirements.quote: In general, State laws that are contrary to the Privacy Rule are preempted by the federal requirements, which means that the federal requirements will apply.

requirements.title: Exception: State laws providing greater privacy protections are not preempted
requirements.description: A contrary State law is excepted from federal preemption where it relates to the privacy of individually identifiable health information and provides greater privacy protections or privacy rights with respect to such information.
requirements.quote: relate to the privacy of individually identifiable health information and provide greater privacy protections or privacy rights with respect to such information

requirements.title: Exception: State public health and vital statistics reporting laws are not preempted
requirements.description: A contrary State law is excepted from preemption where it provides for the reporting of disease or injury, child abuse, birth, or death, or for public health surveillance, investigation, or intervention.
requirements.quote: provide for the reporting of disease or injury, child abuse, birth, or death, or for public health surveillance, investigation, or intervention

requirements.title: Exception: State health plan reporting requirements are not preempted
requirements.description: A contrary State law is excepted from preemption where it requires certain health plan reporting, such as for management or financial audits.
requirements.quote: require certain health plan reporting, such as for management or financial audits

requirements.title: HHS exception determination: fraud and abuse prevention
requirements.description: Preemption of a contrary State law will not occur if HHS determines the State law is necessary to prevent fraud and abuse related to the provision of or payment for health care.
requirements.quote: Is necessary to prevent fraud and abuse related to the provision of or payment for health care,

requirements.title: HHS exception determination: State regulation of insurance and health plans
requirements.description: Preemption will not occur if HHS determines the State law is necessary to ensure appropriate State regulation of insurance and health plans, to the extent expressly authorized by statute or regulation.
requirements.quote: Is necessary to ensure appropriate State regulation of insurance and health plans to the extent expressly authorized by statute or regulation,

requirements.title: HHS exception determination: State reporting on health care delivery or costs
requirements.description: Preemption will not occur if HHS determines the State law is necessary for State reporting on health care delivery or costs.
requirements.quote: Is necessary for State reporting on health care delivery or costs,

requirements.title: HHS exception determination: compelling public health, safety or welfare need
requirements.description: Preemption will not occur if HHS determines the State law is necessary for purposes of serving a compelling public health, safety, or welfare need; where a Privacy Rule provision is at issue, the Secretary must also determine that the intrusion into privacy is warranted when balanced against the need to be served.
requirements.quote: Is necessary for purposes of serving a compelling public health, safety, or welfare need, and, if a Privacy Rule provision is at issue, if the Secretary determines that the intrusion into privacy is warranted when balanced against the need to be served; or

requirements.title: HHS exception determination: controlled substances regulation
requirements.description: Preemption will not occur if HHS determines the State law has as its principal purpose the regulation of the manufacture, registration, distribution, dispensing, or other control of any controlled substances, or of substances deemed controlled substances by State law.
requirements.quote: Has as its principal purpose the regulation of the manufacture, registration, distribution, dispensing, or other control of any controlled substances, or that is deemed a controlled substance by State law.

requirements.title: HHS determination process for preemption exceptions
requirements.description: HHS is the body that determines whether a contrary State law qualifies for an exception to federal preemption under the listed grounds.
requirements.quote: Preemption of a contrary State law will not occur if HHS determines that the State law:
requirements.trigger: A contrary State law is asserted to qualify for an exception to federal preemption
requirements.happyPath: HHS reviews the contrary State law against the exception grounds and determines whether preemption occurs; where a Privacy Rule provision is at issue, the Secretary balances the intrusion into privacy against the need to be served.

requirements.title: HHS voluntary compliance cooperation and technical assistance
requirements.description: HHS seeks the cooperation of covered entities and may provide technical assistance to help them comply voluntarily with the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: HHS will seek the cooperation of covered entities and may provide technical assistance to help them comply voluntarily with the Rule.

requirements.title: Complaint filing process with HHS
requirements.description: The Privacy Rule must provide processes by which persons can file complaints with HHS regarding a covered entity's compliance.
requirements.quote: The Rule provides processes for persons to file complaints with HHS

requirements.title: Covered entity must provide records and compliance reports and cooperate with investigations
requirements.description: Covered entities are responsible for providing records and compliance reports, cooperating with investigations and compliance reviews, and permitting access to information for those purposes.
requirements.quote: describes the responsibilities of covered entities to provide records and compliance reports and to cooperate with, and permit access to information for, investigations and compliance reviews

requirements.title: Civil money penalty of $100 per failure to comply
requirements.description: HHS may impose a civil money penalty on a covered entity of $100 for each failure to comply with a Privacy Rule requirement.
requirements.quote: HHS may impose civil money penalties on a covered entity of $100 per failure to comply with a Privacy Rule requirement.

requirements.title: Annual cap of $25,000 for identical violations
requirements.description: The civil money penalty may not exceed $25,000 per calendar year for multiple violations of the identical Privacy Rule requirement.
requirements.quote: That penalty may not exceed $25,000 per year for multiple violations of the identical Privacy Rule requirement in a calendar year.

requirements.title: Penalty exception for reasonable cause corrected within 30 days
requirements.description: HHS may not impose a civil money penalty where the violation is due to reasonable cause, did not involve willful neglect, and the covered entity corrected the violation within 30 days of when it knew or should have known of the violation.
requirements.quote: HHS may not impose a civil money penalty under specific circumstances, such as when a violation is due to reasonable cause and did not involve willful neglect and the covered entity corrected the violation within 30 days of when it knew or should have known of the violation.
requirements.trigger: A Privacy Rule violation occurs due to reasonable cause without willful neglect
requirements.happyPath: The covered entity discovers the violation and corrects it within 30 days, avoiding a civil money penalty.

requirements.title: Criminal penalty for knowing wrongful disclosure
requirements.description: A person who knowingly obtains or discloses individually identifiable health information in violation of HIPAA faces a fine of $50,000 and up to one-year imprisonment.
requirements.quote: A person who knowingly obtains or discloses individually identifiable health information in violation of HIPAA faces a fine of $50,000 and up to one-year imprisonment.

requirements.title: Enhanced criminal penalty for false pretenses
requirements.description: Criminal penalties increase to $100,000 and up to five years imprisonment where the wrongful conduct involves false pretenses.
requirements.quote: The criminal penalties increase to $100,000 and up to five years imprisonment if the wrongful conduct involves false pretenses

requirements.title: Maximum criminal penalty for commercial advantage or malicious harm
requirements.description: Criminal penalties increase to $250,000 and up to ten years imprisonment where the wrongful conduct involves intent to sell, transfer, or use individually identifiable health information for commercial advantage, personal gain, or malicious harm.
requirements.quote: and to $250,000 and up to ten years imprisonment if the wrongful conduct involves the intent to sell, transfer, or use individually identifiable health information for commercial advantage, personal gain, or malicious harm

requirements.title: Criminal sanctions enforced by Department of Justice
requirements.description: Enforcement of HIPAA criminal sanctions is the responsibility of the Department of Justice rather than HHS.
requirements.quote: Criminal sanctions will be enforced by the Department of Justice.

requirements.title: Privacy Rule compliance deadline for covered entities
requirements.description: All covered entities other than small health plans must achieve compliance with the HIPAA Privacy Rule by April 14, 2003.
requirements.quote: All covered entities, except "small health plans," must be compliant with the Privacy Rule by April 14, 2003.

requirements.title: Extended compliance deadline for small health plans
requirements.description: Small health plans are given an additional year, until April 14, 2004, to comply with the Privacy Rule.
requirements.quote: Small health plans, however, have until April 14, 2004 to comply.

requirements.title: Definition of a small health plan
requirements.description: A health plan qualifies as a small health plan if its annual receipts are not more than $5 million.
requirements.quote: A health plan with annual receipts of not more than $5 million is a small health plan.

requirements.title: Safe harbor de-identification requires removal of 18 identifier categories
requirements.description: To de-identify PHI using the safe harbor method under 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b), all listed identifiers of the individual and of relatives, employers, or household members must be removed, including names, telephone and fax numbers, email addresses, social security numbers, medical record numbers, health plan beneficiary numbers, account numbers, certificate/license numbers, vehicle and device identifiers, URLs, IP addresses, biometric identifiers, full face photographic images, and any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code.
requirements.quote: The following identifiers of the individual or of relatives, employers, or household members of the individual must be removed to achieve the "safe harbor" method of de-identification (45 C.F.R. § 164.514(b)):

requirements.title: Geographic subdivision and three-digit zip code rule
requirements.description: All geographic subdivisions smaller than a State must be removed, except the initial three digits of a zip code where the combined geographic unit contains more than 20,000 people; for units of 20,000 or fewer people, the initial three digits must be changed to 000.
requirements.quote: (B) All geographic subdivisions smaller than a State, including street address, city, county, precinct, zip code, and their equivalent geocodes, except for the initial three digits of a zip code if the geographic units formed by combining all zip codes with the same three initial digits contains more than 20,000 people, and the initial three digits of a zip code for all such geographic units containing 20,000 or fewer people is changed to 000;

requirements.title: Date elements and age over 89 handling
requirements.description: All elements of dates except year that relate directly to the individual (birth date, admission date, discharge date, date of death) must be removed, and all ages over 89 and date elements indicative of such age must be removed or aggregated into a single category of age 90 or older.
requirements.quote: (C) All elements of dates (except year) for dates directly related to the individual, including birth date, admission date, discharge date, date of death; and all ages over 89 and all elements of dates (including year) indicative of such age, except that such ages and elements may be aggregated into a single category of age 90 or older;

requirements.title: No actual knowledge of re-identification risk
requirements.description: Beyond removing the listed identifiers, the covered entity must not have actual knowledge that the remaining information could be used alone or in combination with other information to identify the subject individual.
requirements.quote: the covered entity may not have actual knowledge that the remaining information could be used alone or in combination with any other information to identify an individual who is subject of the information

requirements.title: Re-identification codes permitted under conditions
requirements.description: Any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code must be removed, except as permitted for re-identification purposes provided certain conditions are met.
requirements.quote: (R) any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code, except as permitted for re-identification purposes provided certain conditions are met

requirements.title: Limited data set must exclude specified direct identifiers
requirements.description: A limited data set is protected health information from which the enumerated direct identifiers listed in 45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e)(2) have been removed. Any data set offered as a limited data set must have all sixteen categories of direct identifiers stripped before use or disclosure.
requirements.quote: A limited data set is protected health information that excludes the following direct identifiers of the individual or of relatives, employers, or household members of the individual (45 C.F.R. § 164.514(e)(2)):

requirements.title: Identifier removal extends to relatives, employers and household members
requirements.description: The exclusion of direct identifiers is not limited to the individual who is the subject of the record. Identifiers belonging to the individual's relatives, employers, or household members must also be removed for the data set to qualify as a limited data set.
requirements.quote: of the individual or of relatives, employers, or household members of the individual

requirements.title: Names and detailed postal address must be removed; town, State and zip code may remain
requirements.description: Names must be excluded from a limited data set. Postal address information must also be excluded, except that town or city, State and zip code may be retained.
requirements.quote: (i) Names; (ii) Postal address information, other than town or city, State and zip code;

requirements.title: Direct contact identifiers must be removed
requirements.description: Telephone numbers, fax numbers and electronic mail addresses are direct identifiers that must be excluded from a limited data set.
requirements.quote: (iii) Telephone numbers; (iv) Fax numbers; (v) Electronic mail addresses;

requirements.title: Government, record, plan and account numbers must be removed
requirements.description: Social security numbers, medical record numbers, health plan beneficiary numbers, account numbers and certificate/license numbers must all be excluded from a limited data set.
requirements.quote: (vi) Social security numbers; (vii) Medical record numbers; (viii) Health plan beneficiary numbers; (ix) Account numbers; (x) Certificate/license numbers;

requirements.title: Vehicle and device identifiers must be removed
requirements.description: Vehicle identifiers and serial numbers (including license plate numbers) and device identifiers and serial numbers must be excluded from a limited data set.
requirements.quote: (xi) Vehicle identifiers and serial numbers, including license plate numbers; (xii) Device identifiers and serial numbers;

requirements.title: Web URLs and IP addresses must be removed
requirements.description: Web Universal Resource Locators (URLs) and Internet Protocol (IP) address numbers are direct identifiers that must be excluded from a limited data set.
requirements.quote: (xiii) Web Universal Resource Locators (URLs); (xiv) Internet Protocol (IP) address numbers;

requirements.title: Biometric identifiers and full face images must be removed
requirements.description: Biometric identifiers, including finger and voice prints, and full face photographic images and any comparable images must be excluded from a limited data set.
requirements.quote: (xv) Biometric identifiers, including finger and voice prints; (xvi) Full face photographic images and any comparable images.

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes must be authored by a mental health professional
requirements.description: Content qualifies as psychotherapy notes only when recorded, in any medium, by a health care provider who is a mental health professional and documents or analyzes the contents of conversation during a private, group, joint, or family counseling session.
requirements.quote: "Psychotherapy notes" means notes recorded (in any medium) by a health care provider who is a mental health professional documenting or analyzing the contents of conversation during a private counseling session or a group, joint, or family counseling session

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes must be separated from the rest of the medical record
requirements.description: To be treated as psychotherapy notes, the notes must be maintained separately from the remainder of the individual's medical record, per 45 C.F.R. § 164.501.
requirements.quote: and that are separated from the rest of the individual's medical record

requirements.title: Medication prescription and monitoring excluded from psychotherapy notes
requirements.description: Records of medication prescription and monitoring are not psychotherapy notes and therefore do not receive the heightened psychotherapy notes protections.
requirements.quote: Psychotherapy notes excludes medication prescription and monitoring

requirements.title: Session start and stop times excluded from psychotherapy notes
requirements.description: Counseling session start and stop times are excluded from the definition of psychotherapy notes.
requirements.quote: counseling session start and stop times

requirements.title: Treatment modalities and frequencies excluded from psychotherapy notes
requirements.description: The modalities and frequencies of treatment furnished are excluded from the definition of psychotherapy notes.
requirements.quote: the modalities and frequencies of treatment furnished

requirements.title: Clinical test results excluded from psychotherapy notes
requirements.description: Results of clinical tests are excluded from the definition of psychotherapy notes.
requirements.quote: results of clinical tests

requirements.title: Summaries of diagnosis, status, plan, symptoms, prognosis and progress excluded
requirements.description: Any summary of diagnosis, functional status, the treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, and progress to date is excluded from the definition of psychotherapy notes.
requirements.quote: any summary of the following items: diagnosis, functional status, the treatment plan, symptoms, prognosis, and progress to date

requirements.title: MVP scope: record access, consent, audit and disclosure
requirements.description: The MVP release of the Patient Data Platform must cover four capability areas: patient record access, consent management, audit, and disclosure handling. Release target is Q3 2025.
requirements.quote: **Scope:** MVP — patient record access, consent management, audit and disclosure handling

requirements.title: Every record access must be accountable
requirements.description: The platform must provide clinicians with fast access to the records they need while ensuring that each access event is accountable and attributable.
requirements.quote: Give clinicians fast access to the records they need while making every access accountable.

requirements.title: Record lookup time reduced from minutes to seconds
requirements.description: The platform must reduce the time required to locate a patient record from minutes to seconds.
requirements.quote: The platform must reduce the time to locate a patient record from minutes to seconds

requirements.title: Surface only access events warranting privacy-officer attention
requirements.description: The platform must reduce privacy-officer review effort by filtering and surfacing only those access events that warrant attention, rather than all access events.
requirements.quote: reduce privacy-officer review effort by surfacing only the access events that warrant attention

requirements.title: Role-based access control by clinical role
requirements.description: Access to record content must be governed by the user's clinical role so staff see only what their job requires. Supported roles: attending clinician, nurse, scheduling clerk, billing analyst, privacy officer, system administrator.
requirements.quote: Roles: attending clinician, nurse, scheduling clerk, billing analyst, privacy officer, system administrator

requirements.title: Role-to-record-section permission mapping
requirements.description: Each role maps to a permitted set of record sections: demographics, encounters, medications, clinical notes, psychotherapy notes, substance use records, and billing.
requirements.quote: Each role maps to a permitted set of record sections: demographics, encounters, medications, clinical notes, psychotherapy notes, substance use records, billing

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes and substance use records excluded by default
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes and substance use records are excluded from every role by default and can only be reached through an explicit per-patient grant.
requirements.quote: Psychotherapy notes and substance use records are excluded from every role by default and require explicit per-patient grant

requirements.title: Dual approval for role assignment
requirements.description: Role assignment must be approved by a second person; the system rejects self-approval.
requirements.quote: Role assignment requires approval by a second person; self-approval is rejected by the system

requirements.title: Access reviews every 90 days
requirements.description: The system generates access reviews every 90 days, listing every user and their effective permissions.
requirements.quote: Access reviews generated every 90 days, listing every user and their effective permissions

requirements.title: Out-of-scope access attempt denied and logged
requirements.description: A scheduling clerk attempting to retrieve a clinical note receives a permission error and the attempt is written to the log.
requirements.quote: A scheduling clerk retrieving a clinical note receives a permission error, and the attempt is logged

requirements.title: No role-level access to psychotherapy notes without authorisation record
requirements.description: No role grants access to psychotherapy notes unless an explicit per-patient authorisation record exists.
requirements.quote: No role grants access to psychotherapy notes without an explicit per-patient authorisation record

requirements.title: Role changes propagate within 60 seconds with approver identity
requirements.description: Role changes must take effect within 60 seconds and be recorded together with the identity of the approver.
requirements.quote: Role changes take effect within 60 seconds and are recorded with approver identity

requirements.title: Access review export contents
requirements.description: The access review export must include user, role, last login and records accessed in the period.
requirements.quote: Access review export includes user, role, last login and records accessed in the period

requirements.title: Emergency clinician uses break-glass to reach an out-of-scope record
requirements.description: An emergency clinician facing a life-at-risk situation invokes break-glass, selects a reason from a fixed list, adds free text, and is granted immediate access to a record outside normal scope so care is not delayed.
requirements.quote: As an emergency clinician, I want to reach a record outside my normal scope when a patient's life is at risk, so that care is not delayed by a permission boundary.
requirements.trigger: A patient's life is at risk and the needed record is outside the clinician's normal access scope
requirements.happyPath: Clinician invokes break-glass, selects a reason from the fixed list and adds free text, access is granted immediately, session runs up to 4 hours, and the event is queued for privacy officer review.

requirements.title: Break-glass requires stated reason from fixed list plus free text
requirements.description: Invoking break-glass access requires the user to select a reason from a fixed list and to supply free text.
requirements.quote: Break-glass requires a stated reason from a fixed list plus free text

requirements.title: Break-glass access granted without approval in the path
requirements.description: Break-glass access is granted immediately, with no approval step in the access path.
requirements.quote: Access granted immediately; no approval in the path

requirements.title: Break-glass session limited to 4 hours
requirements.description: A break-glass session is limited to 4 hours, after which re-authorisation is required.
requirements.quote: Session limited to 4 hours, then re-authorisation required

requirements.title: Break-glass events queued for privacy officer review
requirements.description: Every break-glass event is queued for review by the privacy officer.
requirements.quote: Every break-glass event queued for privacy officer review

requirements.title: Patient notified of break-glass access within 30 days
requirements.description: The patient must be notified of break-glass access to their record within 30 days.
requirements.quote: Patient notified of break-glass access to their record within 30 days

requirements.title: Break-glass access granted in under 5 seconds
requirements.description: Break-glass must grant access in under 5 seconds, since delay constitutes a clinical risk.
requirements.quote: Break-glass grants access in under 5 seconds — a delay here is a clinical risk

requirements.title: Break-glass events reach review queue within 60 seconds
requirements.description: Every break-glass event must appear in the privacy officer review queue within 60 seconds.
requirements.quote: Every event appears in the privacy officer queue within 60 seconds

requirements.title: No bulk dismissal of break-glass review queue
requirements.description: The review queue cannot be dismissed in bulk; each break-glass event requires an individual decision.
requirements.quote: Review queue cannot be dismissed in bulk; each event requires an individual decision

requirements.title: Break-glass audit trail contents
requirements.description: The break-glass audit trail must capture user, patient, reason, records viewed, duration, reviewer and outcome.
requirements.quote: Audit trail: user, patient, reason, records viewed, duration, reviewer, outcome

requirements.title: Record consents and authorisations against the patient
requirements.description: The system shall record patient consents and authorisations against the patient record so that disclosures can be automatically checked against them.
requirements.quote: As a health information manager, I want consents and authorisations recorded against the patient so that disclosures can be checked against them automatically.
requirements.trigger: A consent or authorisation is obtained from a patient
requirements.happyPath: The health information manager records the consent against the patient; subsequent disclosure attempts are automatically checked against the recorded consent.

requirements.title: Supported consent types
requirements.description: The system must support the following consent types: general treatment consent, research participation, marketing, substance use disorder disclosure (42 CFR Part 2), and psychotherapy notes authorisation.
requirements.quote: Consent types: general treatment consent, research participation, marketing, substance use disorder disclosure (42 CFR Part 2), psychotherapy notes authorisation

requirements.title: Mandatory consent record attributes
requirements.description: Each consent record must capture scope, recipient class, purpose, effective date, expiry date, and method of capture.
requirements.quote: Each consent records: scope, recipient class, purpose, effective date, expiry date, and method of capture

requirements.title: Consents are revocable with immediate effect
requirements.description: Consents must be revocable. Revocation takes effect immediately for future disclosures and is recorded together with a timestamp.
requirements.quote: Consents are revocable; revocation is effective immediately for future disclosures and recorded with a timestamp

requirements.title: Expired consent blocks disclosure but not treatment access
requirements.description: An expired consent must not block treatment access, but must block the specific disclosure that the consent governed.
requirements.quote: Expired consents must not block treatment access, but must block the disclosure they governed

requirements.title: Disclosure without active consent is refused and logged
requirements.description: When a disclosure is attempted and no matching active consent exists, the system refuses the disclosure and writes a log entry.
requirements.quote: A disclosure attempt without a matching active consent is refused and logged

requirements.title: Revocation propagates within 60 seconds
requirements.description: A consent revocation must be reflected in disclosure checks within 60 seconds of being recorded.
requirements.quote: Revocation propagates to disclosure checks within 60 seconds

requirements.title: Part 2 consent required for substance use disorder disclosure
requirements.description: Substance use disorder records may not be disclosed unless a 42 CFR Part 2 consent is present; a general consent is never sufficient.
requirements.quote: Substance use disorder records cannot be disclosed without a Part 2 consent, regardless of any general consent

requirements.title: Full consent history retained; revoked consents never deleted
requirements.description: The complete history of consents must be retained, and a revoked consent must never be deleted from the record.
requirements.quote: Consent history is retained in full; a revoked consent is never deleted

requirements.title: Audit entry generated for every PHI access event
requirements.description: The system must generate an audit entry for every read, write, export and print action performed on PHI.
requirements.quote: Every read, write, export and print of PHI generates an audit entry

requirements.title: Required audit entry fields
requirements.description: Each audit entry must contain user identity, role at time of access, patient identifier, record section, action, timestamp, source IP, and outcome.
requirements.quote: Entry contains: user identity, role at time of access, patient identifier, record section, action, timestamp, source IP, and outcome

requirements.title: Append-only audit storage
requirements.description: Audit storage must be append-only, with no application path permitting update or deletion of audit records.
requirements.quote: Audit storage is append-only; no application path permits update or delete

requirements.title: Audit retention of at least 6 years
requirements.description: Audit records are retained for a minimum of 6 years, with configuration for longer retention in states requiring it.
requirements.quote: Retention 6 years minimum, configurable higher for states requiring longer

requirements.title: Audit records queryable by patient, user and date range
requirements.description: The system must support querying audit records by patient, by user and by date range.
requirements.quote: Audit records queryable by patient, by user and by date range

requirements.title: Compliance officer answers auditor from audit log
requirements.description: A compliance officer uses the complete, tamper-evident PHI access record to respond to an auditor without reconstructing data.
requirements.quote: As a compliance officer, I want a complete and tamper-evident record of PHI access so that I can answer an auditor without reconstructing anything.
requirements.trigger: An auditor requests evidence of PHI access
requirements.happyPath: The compliance officer queries the immutable audit log by patient, user or date range and exports a signed file for the auditor.

requirements.title: Synchronous audit write blocks unlogged access
requirements.description: The audit write must be synchronous with the access it records; an access that cannot be logged must fail rather than proceed unlogged.
requirements.quote: Audit write is synchronous with the access it records — an access that cannot be logged must fail rather than proceed unlogged

requirements.title: Patient access history query under 3 seconds
requirements.description: A query for one patient's full access history must return in under 3 seconds.
requirements.quote: Query for one patient's full access history returns in under 3 seconds

requirements.title: No interface permits modification of audit rows
requirements.description: No API, admin console or database role may permit modification of an existing audit row.
requirements.quote: No API, admin console or database role permits modification of an existing audit row

requirements.title: Signed audit export file
requirements.description: Audit export must produce a signed file suitable for submission to an auditor.
requirements.quote: Export produces a signed file suitable for submission to an auditor

requirements.title: Per-user access baseline
requirements.description: The system establishes a baseline per user covering records per day, departments touched, and hours of activity.
requirements.quote: Baseline per user: records per day, departments touched, hours of activity

requirements.title: Flag same-surname patient access
requirements.description: Access to a record for a patient with the same surname as the user must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: access to a record for a patient with the same surname as the user

requirements.title: Flag VIP or employee record access
requirements.description: Access to a VIP or employee record must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: access to a VIP or employee record

requirements.title: Flag volume above three standard deviations
requirements.description: Access volume more than three standard deviations above the user's baseline must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: volume more than three standard deviations above the user's baseline

requirements.title: Flag off-hours access
requirements.description: Access outside the user's normal hours must be flagged where the user has an established pattern.
requirements.quote: Flag: access outside the user's normal hours, where the user has an established pattern

requirements.title: Flag access with no recorded care relationship
requirements.description: A record accessed by a user with no care relationship recorded must be flagged.
requirements.quote: Flag: a record accessed by a user with no care relationship recorded

requirements.title: Privacy officer reviews surfaced anomalous access
requirements.description: A privacy officer reviews unusual access surfaced by anomaly detection rather than reading every log line.
requirements.quote: As a privacy officer, I want unusual access surfaced so that I review what matters instead of reading every log line.
requirements.trigger: An anomalous PHI access is detected
requirements.happyPath: The system flags the access with reason and evidence, the privacy officer reviews it, and the decision feeds back into the baseline.

requirements.title: Flags raised within 30 minutes
requirements.description: Anomaly flags must be raised within 30 minutes of the access.
requirements.quote: Flags raised within 30 minutes of the access

requirements.title: False positive rate below 20%
requirements.description: The anomaly detection false positive rate must remain below 20%, measured monthly against reviewer outcomes.
requirements.quote: False positive rate below 20%, measured monthly against reviewer outcomes

requirements.title: Flags include reason and triggering evidence
requirements.description: Each anomaly flag must carry the reason it was raised and the evidence that triggered it.
requirements.quote: Each flag carries the reason and the evidence that triggered it

requirements.title: Reviewer decisions feed back into baseline
requirements.description: Decisions made by reviewers on flags must feed back into the user baseline.
requirements.quote: Reviewer decisions feed back into the baseline

requirements.title: Track access requests against the statutory 30-day clock
requirements.description: A health information manager needs to track right-of-access requests end to end against the statutory clock so the 30-day deadline is never missed, from intake and identity verification through assembly and delivery.
requirements.quote: As a health information manager, I want to track access requests against the statutory clock so that we do not miss the 30-day deadline.
requirements.trigger: A patient submits a right of access request
requirements.happyPath: Request is received and recorded, patient identity is verified, the clock is tracked with days remaining, the designated record set is assembled excluding psychotherapy notes, and the records are delivered by the requested method within 30 days.

requirements.title: Capture request intake details
requirements.description: On intake the system must record the patient identity and the verification method used, the scope of records requested, the format requested, and the date the request was received.
requirements.quote: Request intake records: patient identity and verification method, scope requested, format requested, date received

requirements.title: Statutory clock starts on receipt
requirements.description: The 30-day response clock begins on the date the request is received, not on the date the patient's identity is verified.
requirements.quote: Clock starts on receipt, not on verification

requirements.title: Single 30-day extension with prior written notice
requirements.description: At most one 30-day extension may be taken on an access request, and it requires written notice to the patient issued before day 30.
requirements.quote: One 30-day extension permitted, requiring written notice to the patient before day 30

requirements.title: Assemble designated record set excluding psychotherapy notes
requirements.description: Fulfilment assembles the designated record set for the requested scope and must exclude psychotherapy notes from what is delivered.
requirements.quote: Fulfilment assembles the designated record set, excluding psychotherapy notes

requirements.title: Supported delivery methods for fulfilled requests
requirements.description: Fulfilled access requests can be delivered by secure portal download, encrypted email, or physical media.
requirements.quote: Delivery methods: secure portal download, encrypted email, physical media

requirements.title: Days remaining shown on open requests
requirements.description: Every open access request displays the number of days remaining against the statutory deadline.
requirements.quote: Days remaining displayed on every open request

requirements.title: Extension blocked without evidence of patient notification
requirements.description: The system must prevent an extension from being recorded unless there is evidence that the patient was notified.
requirements.quote: Extension cannot be recorded without evidence the patient was notified

requirements.title: Escalate requests approaching day 25
requirements.description: Access requests that reach day 25 are escalated to the health information manager.
requirements.quote: Requests approaching day 25 escalate to the health information manager

requirements.title: End-to-end audit trail for access requests
requirements.description: The audit trail must cover the request, the verification, the assembly, the delivery, and the identity of every actor involved.
requirements.quote: Audit trail: request, verification, assembly, delivery, and the identity of every actor

requirements.title: Patient request for accounting of disclosures
requirements.description: A patient can request a list of the parties their information was disclosed to, so they can see where their information has gone.
requirements.quote: As a patient, I want a list of who my information was disclosed to, so that I can see where it has gone.
requirements.trigger: Patient submits a request for an accounting of disclosures
requirements.happyPath: The request is logged, the system compiles qualifying disclosures from the six years prior to the request excluding treatment, payment and healthcare operations, and a patient-readable accounting is delivered within 60 days.

requirements.title: Accounting covers six years prior to request
requirements.description: The accounting of disclosures must span the six-year period preceding the date of the patient's request.
requirements.quote: Accounting covers six years prior to the request

requirements.title: Exclude treatment, payment and operations disclosures
requirements.description: Disclosures made for treatment, payment or healthcare operations are excluded from the accounting.
requirements.quote: Excludes treatment, payment and healthcare operations disclosures

requirements.title: Required content of each accounting entry
requirements.description: Each accounting entry must include the date of disclosure, the recipient's name and address, a description of the PHI disclosed, and the purpose of the disclosure.
requirements.quote: Includes: date, recipient name and address, description of PHI, and purpose

requirements.title: First accounting free in a 12-month period
requirements.description: The first accounting of disclosures in any 12-month period is provided free of charge; subsequent requests may carry a cost-based fee provided notice is given.
requirements.quote: First accounting in any 12-month period is free; subsequent requests may carry a cost-based fee after notice

requirements.title: Accounting produced within 60 days
requirements.description: The accounting of disclosures must be generated within 60 days of receiving the patient's request.
requirements.quote: Accounting generated within 60 days of request

requirements.title: Exclusions verified by sampling
requirements.description: Excluded disclosure categories must be genuinely absent from the accounting output, and this is verified by sampling.
requirements.quote: Excluded categories are genuinely excluded, verified by sampling

requirements.title: Accounting output is patient-readable
requirements.description: The accounting output must be readable by a patient rather than presented as a raw system log.
requirements.quote: Output is readable by a patient, not a system log

requirements.title: Structured incident-to-breach notification decision workflow
requirements.description: Privacy officer follows a structured path from a suspected privacy incident through the four-factor assessment to a notification decision, ensuring the assessment step cannot be bypassed.
requirements.quote: As a privacy officer, I want a structured path from a suspected incident to a notification decision, so that the four-factor assessment is never skipped.
requirements.trigger: A suspected privacy incident is identified
requirements.happyPath: Incident is intaken, four-factor risk assessment is recorded, breach determination is made with reasoning, affected individuals are assembled, and notifications are issued or the incident is closed as non-reportable

requirements.title: Multi-channel incident intake
requirements.description: The system must accept incident intake from anomaly flags, staff reports, patient complaints and vendor notifications.
requirements.quote: Incident intake from: anomaly flags, staff report, patient complaint, vendor notification

requirements.title: Explicit four-factor risk assessment capture
requirements.description: The system must record the four-factor risk assessment explicitly: nature and extent of PHI, who received it, whether it was acquired or viewed, and mitigation.
requirements.quote: Four-factor risk assessment recorded explicitly: nature and extent of PHI, who received it, whether it was acquired or viewed, and mitigation

requirements.title: Presumption of breach unless low probability of compromise
requirements.description: An incident is presumed to be a breach unless the four-factor assessment concludes there is a low probability of compromise, and the reasoning for that conclusion is recorded.
requirements.quote: Presumption of breach unless the assessment concludes low probability of compromise, with reasoning recorded

requirements.title: Affected individual list built from audit records
requirements.description: The system must assemble the list of affected individuals for a breach from audit records.
requirements.quote: Affected individual list assembled from audit records

requirements.title: Notification templates for individual, HHS and media
requirements.description: The system must provide breach notification templates for affected individuals, HHS and media notices.
requirements.quote: Notification templates for individual, HHS and media

requirements.title: Non-reportable closure blocked without all four factors
requirements.description: The system must prevent closing a breach as non-reportable unless all four assessment factors have been recorded.
requirements.quote: A breach cannot be closed as non-reportable without all four factors recorded

requirements.title: 60-day notification countdown from discovery
requirements.description: The system must display a countdown from the discovery date against a 60-day notification deadline.
requirements.quote: Countdown from discovery date displayed, 60-day deadline

requirements.title: Breaches affecting 500 or more individuals flagged
requirements.description: Breaches involving 500 or more affected individuals must be flagged for the separate HHS timeline and media notice.
requirements.quote: Breaches of 500 or more individuals flagged for the separate HHS timeline and media notice

requirements.title: Business associate discovery date recorded
requirements.description: Business associate notifications must be recorded using the date the associate discovered the incident, not the date the associate reported it to the covered entity.
requirements.quote: Business associate notifications recorded with the date the associate discovered the incident, not the date they told us

requirements.title: Record retrieval performance at 95th percentile
requirements.description: The system must return patient record retrievals in under 2 seconds measured at the 95th percentile.
requirements.quote: Record retrieval under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile

requirements.title: Break-glass grant latency under 5 seconds
requirements.description: When break-glass emergency access is invoked, the access grant must complete in under 5 seconds.
requirements.quote: Break-glass grant under 5 seconds

requirements.title: Single-patient audit query under 3 seconds
requirements.description: An audit trail query scoped to a single patient must return results in under 3 seconds.
requirements.quote: Audit query for one patient under 3 seconds

requirements.title: Minimum concurrent clinical user capacity
requirements.description: The system must support a minimum of 200 concurrent clinical users.
requirements.quote: 200 concurrent clinical users minimum

requirements.title: Encryption at rest using AES-256
requirements.description: Data stored by the system must be encrypted at rest using AES-256.
requirements.quote: Encryption at rest AES-256, in transit TLS 1.2 or higher

requirements.title: Encryption in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher
requirements.description: All data transmitted by the system must be protected in transit using TLS version 1.2 or higher.
requirements.quote: Encryption at rest AES-256, in transit TLS 1.2 or higher

requirements.title: Unique user identification with no shared accounts
requirements.description: Every user must have a unique identity; shared accounts are prohibited and this prohibition must be enforced by the system itself rather than by policy alone.
requirements.quote: Unique user identification; no shared accounts, enforced by the system

requirements.title: Automatic logoff after 15 minutes of inactivity
requirements.description: Clinical workstation sessions must be automatically terminated after 15 minutes of user inactivity.
requirements.quote: Automatic logoff after 15 minutes of inactivity on clinical workstations

requirements.title: Key management separated from data storage with documented rotation
requirements.description: Encryption key management must be architecturally separated from data storage, and key rotation procedures must be documented.
requirements.quote: Key management separated from data storage with documented rotation

requirements.title: Multi-factor authentication for remote access
requirements.description: Remote access to the system must require multi-factor authentication.
requirements.quote: Multi-factor authentication for remote access

requirements.title: 99.9% platform uptime
requirements.description: The platform must maintain 99.9% uptime, reflecting that clinical systems cannot be unavailable while care is being delivered.
requirements.quote: 99.9% uptime; clinical systems cannot be unavailable during care

requirements.title: Recovery time objective of 4 hours
requirements.description: Following an outage or disaster, the platform must be restored to service within a recovery time objective of 4 hours.
requirements.quote: Recovery time objective 4 hours, recovery point objective 15 minutes

requirements.title: Recovery point objective of 15 minutes
requirements.description: Data loss in a recovery scenario must not exceed 15 minutes, requiring backup/replication frequency sufficient to meet a 15-minute recovery point objective.
requirements.quote: Recovery time objective 4 hours, recovery point objective 15 minutes

requirements.title: Documented emergency mode operation procedures
requirements.description: Emergency mode operation must be documented so that clinical work can continue when the platform is unavailable.
requirements.quote: Documented emergency mode operation when the platform is unavailable

requirements.title: Minimum necessary enforcement at record-section level
requirements.description: The system must enforce the minimum necessary principle with granularity down to individual record sections, not just whole records.
requirements.quote: Minimum necessary enforced at record-section level

requirements.title: Safe Harbor de-identification for research extracts
requirements.description: The platform must provide de-identification of data for research extracts using the Safe Harbor method.
requirements.quote: De-identification available for research extracts, using the Safe Harbor method

requirements.title: GDPR erasure requests for EU patients
requirements.description: Erasure requests from EU patients must be honoured, except where a legal retention obligation applies to the data.
requirements.quote: GDPR: erasure requests honoured for EU patients where no legal retention obligation applies

requirements.title: Patient-to-patient messaging excluded from MVP
requirements.description: Direct messaging between patients is explicitly out of scope for the MVP release; the system will not provide patient-to-patient message exchange in the initial delivery.
requirements.quote: Direct patient-to-patient messaging

requirements.title: Genomic data storage excluded from MVP
requirements.description: The MVP will not store genomic data. Any genomic data handling capability is deferred beyond the initial release.
requirements.quote: Genomic data storage

requirements.title: Clinical decision support excluded from MVP
requirements.description: Clinical decision support functionality is out of scope for the MVP and will not be implemented in the initial release.
requirements.quote: Clinical decision support

requirements.title: Automated expert-determination de-identification excluded from MVP
requirements.description: The MVP will not include automated de-identification based on the expert determination method. De-identification via expert determination is deferred and remains an open question.
requirements.quote: Automated de-identification using expert determination

requirements.title: Multi-state, multi-facility scale support
requirements.description: The platform must support an organization operating 4 hospitals and 31 outpatient clinics across three states, serving approximately 480,000 patients per year.
requirements.quote: Meridian Regional Health operates 4 hospitals and 31 outpatient clinics across three states, serving roughly 480,000 patients a year.

requirements.title: Audit inquiries answerable without manual reconstruction
requirements.description: The replacement platform must be able to answer an auditor's questions directly, eliminating the multi-day manual reconstruction required by the legacy records platform.
requirements.quote: It is replacing a records platform that cannot answer an auditor's questions without a manual reconstruction taking days.

requirements.title: Anomaly-focused access log review
requirements.description: Access log monitoring must surface only anomalous access events for human review, replacing the current practice of the privacy team reading access logs line by line for most of the week.
requirements.quote: The target is that they read only what is anomalous, and that a right-of-access request is fulfilled in days rather than the current average of 26.

requirements.title: Right-of-access request fulfilled in days
requirements.description: A patient right-of-access request must be fulfilled within days, improving on the current average fulfillment time of 26 (days).
requirements.quote: The target is that they read only what is anomalous, and that a right-of-access request is fulfilled in days rather than the current average of 26.

requirements.title: Privacy team reviews flagged access activity
requirements.description: The privacy team, which currently spends most of its week reading access logs line by line, should instead review only access activity flagged as anomalous by the platform.
requirements.quote: The current privacy team spends most of its week reading access logs line by line.
requirements.trigger: Access log activity is generated by workforce users viewing records
requirements.happyPath: The platform monitors access logs, flags anomalous access events, and the privacy team reviews only the flagged subset instead of every log line.

requirements.title: Dual HIPAA role: covered entity and business associate
requirements.description: MRH operates as a covered entity under HIPAA while simultaneously acting as a business associate for two payer partners, so the compliance programme must satisfy both sets of obligations concurrently.
requirements.quote: Covered entity under HIPAA; also a business associate for two payer partners

requirements.title: Retention statute of 7 years in one state
requirements.description: One of the three states in which MRH operates imposes a 7-year record retention statute that must be applied to records governed by that state's law.
requirements.quote: Three state retention statutes: 7 years, 10 years, and 10 years past the age of majority for minors

requirements.title: Retention statute of 10 years in one state
requirements.description: One of the three states in which MRH operates imposes a 10-year record retention statute that must be applied to records governed by that state's law.
requirements.quote: Three state retention statutes: 7 years, 10 years, and 10 years past the age of majority for minors

requirements.title: Retention of minors' records to 10 years past age of majority
requirements.description: One state statute requires records for minors to be retained for 10 years past the age of majority, meaning retention clocks for minor patients must be calculated from date of majority rather than date of service.
requirements.quote: Three state retention statutes: 7 years, 10 years, and 10 years past the age of majority for minors

requirements.title: Per-state retention rules across three states
requirements.description: MRH operates 4 hospitals and 31 clinics across 3 states, each of which has its own retention statute, so retention handling must be determined by the governing state rather than applied uniformly.
requirements.quote: 4 hospitals, 31 clinics, 3 states (each with its own retention statute)

requirements.title: 42 CFR Part 2 obligations for behavioural health service line
requirements.description: The behavioural health service line brings 42 CFR Part 2 substance use disorder confidentiality obligations into scope for MRH.
requirements.quote: Behavioural health service line, bringing 42 CFR Part 2 obligations

requirements.title: GDPR scope for EU patients at one facility
requirements.description: EU patients treated at one facility near an international airport bring GDPR into scope for a small population, requiring GDPR handling for that subset of records.
requirements.quote: EU patients treated at one facility near an international airport, bringing GDPR into scope for a small population

requirements.title: HITECH breach notification obligations
requirements.description: MRH's regulatory environment includes HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules together with HITECH breach notification requirements.
requirements.quote: HIPAA Privacy and Security Rules, HITECH breach notification

requirements.title: Joint Commission accreditation survey in 2026
requirements.description: A Joint Commission accreditation survey is scheduled for 2026, setting a fixed deadline for evidence and documentation readiness.
requirements.quote: Joint Commission accreditation survey scheduled for 2026

requirements.title: Annual security attestation for two payer contracts
requirements.description: Two payer contracts require MRH to produce a security attestation each year.
requirements.quote: Two payer contracts requiring annual security attestation

requirements.title: Access governance for approximately 6,200 PHI-touching staff
requirements.description: Of MRH's 11,000 staff, roughly 6,200 touch PHI, defining the population that must be covered by access controls and privacy oversight.
requirements.quote: 11,000 staff, of whom roughly 6,200 touch PHI

requirements.title: Privacy team capacity constraint
requirements.description: The privacy function consists of 4 analysts and 1 privacy officer, a fixed capacity against which all monitoring and review workload must be sized.
requirements.quote: Privacy team: 4 analysts and 1 privacy officer

requirements.title: Attending clinician full clinical record access for own panel
requirements.description: Attending clinicians (physicians and advanced practice providers) are granted access to the full clinical record for patients in their care, and records for their panel are available without any further approval step.
requirements.quote: Records for their panel are available without further approval

requirements.title: Break-glass required for records outside the clinician's panel
requirements.description: When an attending clinician needs to access a record for a patient outside their assigned panel, the access must go through the break-glass path and the clinician must supply a stated reason.
requirements.quote: A record outside the panel requires break-glass with a stated reason

requirements.title: Privacy officer review of break-glass events within 5 business days
requirements.description: Every break-glass access event generated by an attending clinician must be reviewed by the privacy officer within 5 business days of the event.
requirements.quote: Privacy officer reviews the break-glass event within 5 business days

requirements.title: Multi-factor authentication for clinician login
requirements.description: Attending clinicians must authenticate with multi-factor authentication when logging in to access PHI.
requirements.quote: Clinician logs in with multi-factor authentication

requirements.title: Same-day provisioning for clinical role on hire
requirements.description: Clinical access for attending clinicians is expected to be provisioned the same day they are hired.
requirements.quote: Expected provisioning time: same day on hire

requirements.title: Clinical role provisioned by identity team after credentialing
requirements.description: The identity team provisions the clinical role only once credentialing for the clinician has completed.
requirements.quote: Credentialing completes and the identity team provisions the clinical role

requirements.title: Attending clinician access journey from credentialing to break-glass review
requirements.description: End-to-end journey for an attending clinician: credentialing completes and the identity team provisions the clinical role; the clinician logs in with MFA; panel records are available without further approval; out-of-panel records require break-glass with a stated reason; and the privacy officer reviews the break-glass event within 5 business days.
requirements.quote: 1. Credentialing completes and the identity team provisions the clinical role
requirements.trigger: Credentialing completes for a newly hired physician or advanced practice provider
requirements.happyPath: Identity team provisions the clinical role same day, clinician authenticates with MFA, accesses their panel records without approval, uses break-glass with a stated reason for out-of-panel records, and the privacy officer reviews that event within 5 business days

requirements.title: Support for shared clinical workstations and personal mobile access
requirements.description: Attending clinicians access PHI from shared clinical workstations and personal mobile devices, so the access model must accommodate both device types.
requirements.quote: Devices: shared clinical workstations and personal mobile

requirements.title: Elevated risk factors for the attending clinician persona
requirements.description: Risk assessment for the attending clinician persona must account for shared workstations, mobile access and high access volume, with an overall access complexity rated Moderate.
requirements.quote: Risk factors: shared workstations, mobile access, high volume

requirements.title: Expected clinician access volume baseline
requirements.description: Attending clinicians access 20-60 records per shift, mostly within their own panel; this is the baseline volume for monitoring and anomaly detection.
requirements.quote: Access pattern: 20-60 records per shift, mostly their own panel

requirements.title: Expected break-glass frequency for clinicians
requirements.description: Break-glass access by attending clinicians is expected only a few times a month, typically originating in the emergency department; the compliance story treats break-glass as the exception path rather than routine access.
requirements.quote: Break-glass needed a few times a month, typically in the emergency department

requirements.title: 42 CFR Part 2 consent required for behavioural health disclosures
requirements.description: Disclosures of substance use disorder treatment records governed by 42 CFR Part 2 require a Part 2 consent, even where a general HIPAA consent would permit the disclosure.
requirements.quote: 42 CFR Part 2 applies: consent required for disclosures a general HIPAA consent would permit

requirements.title: Psychotherapy notes require separate authorisation and are excluded from right of access
requirements.description: Psychotherapy notes must be governed by a separate authorisation and must not be released under a patient's right of access.
requirements.quote: Psychotherapy notes require separate authorisation and are excluded from the right of access

requirements.title: Substance use records must be segregable
requirements.description: The system must hold substance use disorder records in a segregable form so that they can be withheld when a general disclosure is made.
requirements.quote: Substance use records must be segregable so they can be withheld from a general disclosure

requirements.title: Same-day provisioning with a second approval for behavioural health clinicians
requirements.description: Behavioural health clinician access is expected to be provisioned the same day, but requires a second approval step before it is granted.
requirements.quote: Expected provisioning time: same day, but with a second approval

requirements.title: Every Part 2 record access is reviewed individually
requirements.description: Access to 42 CFR Part 2 records must be reviewed in full for every access event rather than through sampling.
requirements.quote: Monitoring: every access to a Part 2 record is reviewed, not sampled

requirements.title: Behavioural health role provisioning requires two approvers
requirements.description: The behavioural health scope role must be provisioned only after two approvers have authorised it.
requirements.quote: Role provisioned with behavioural health scope, requiring two approvers

requirements.title: Part 2 records visible only with patient-specific Part 2 consent
requirements.description: The system must make Part 2 records visible only where a valid Part 2 consent exists for that specific patient.
requirements.quote: Part 2 records visible only where a Part 2 consent exists for that patient

requirements.title: Disclosure requests checked against consent before release
requirements.description: Every disclosure request for behavioural health records must be validated against the applicable consent before any information is released.
requirements.quote: Any disclosure request checked against consent before release

requirements.title: Redisclosure prohibition attached to outgoing Part 2 records
requirements.description: A redisclosure prohibition notice must be attached to every Part 2 record that leaves the system.
requirements.quote: Redisclosure prohibition attached to every Part 2 record leaving the system

requirements.title: Behavioural health access review is individual, not sampled
requirements.description: Reviews of behavioural health clinician access must examine each access event individually rather than applying a sampling approach.
requirements.quote: Access reviewed individually, not by sampling

requirements.title: Behavioural health clinician access to sensitive records
